Reversing the selected eigenline negates both logarithms and the coefficient vector. Forgetting this selection gives the intrinsic generalized invariant in $(\mathbb R^2/\{g\sim-g\})\cup\{\infty\}$; the unquotiented sphere is its signed parameter space. A primitive integral pair $(p_i,q_i)$ is an ordinary smooth filling coefficient. If a realized generalized parameter lies on the ray $g_i=r_i(p_i,q_i)$ with $r_i>0$ and $(p_i,q_i)$ primitive integral, its topological core direction is the ordinary slope $(p_i,q_i)$ and its cone angle is $2\pi/r_i$. before.statement: Let $K_8$ be the standard figure-eight knot, let $E_{K_8}$ be the exterior obtained by deleting the binding neighborhood from its open-book presentation, and use the positive meridian $\mu$ and preferred longitude $\lambda$. The exterior admits a complete finite-volume hyperbolic metric obtained by gluing two regular ideal tetrahedra, of total volume $2v_3=6\Lambda(\pi/3)\approx2.02988$, where $v_3=3\Lambda(\pi/3)$ is the volume of one regular ideal tetrahedron and $\Lambda$ is the Lobachevsky function. The ordinary zero filling along $\lambda$ is a torus bundle over $S^1$ with monodromy matrix $\begin{pmatrix}2&1\\1&1\end{pmatrix}$ on the capped fiber homology, and the filled manifold admits no complete hyperbolic metric.

before.statement: Use the standard PL three-sphere given by the boundary of a fixed PL four-simplex and the product PL structure on $S^3\times I$. A PL map is a map that is affine on every simplex after finite subdivisions of triangulated domain and target. An oriented PL knot is the image of a PL embedding of an oriented triangulated circle into this PL three-sphere. Two such knots are PL concordant when a PL embedding of a triangulated annulus into $S^3\times I$ has them as its lower and upper boundary circles with boundary orientation $-K_0\times\{0\}\sqcup K_1\times\{1\}$, and the embedding is proper, locally flat in the PL category, and has PL product collars at the two boundary circles. PL local-flatness means that each interior pair chart is PL-homeomorphic to $(\mathbb R^4,\mathbb R^2)$ and each boundary pair chart is PL-homeomorphic to $(\mathbb R^4_+,\mathbb R^2_+)$. Annuli with cone singularities or other non-locally-flat points are excluded. This definition makes no assertion identifying PL concordance with smooth or locally flat topological concordance.

after.statement: Use the standard PL three-sphere given by the boundary of a fixed PL four-simplex and the product PL structure on $S^3\times I$. A PL map is a map that is affine on every simplex after finite subdivisions of triangulated domain and target. An oriented PL knot is the image of a PL embedding of an oriented triangulated circle into this PL three-sphere. Two such knots are PL concordant when a PL embedding of a triangulated annulus into $S^3\times I$ has them as its lower and upper boundary circles with boundary orientation $-K_0\times\{0\}\sqcup K_1\times\{1\}$, and the embedding is proper, locally flat in the PL category, and has PL product collars agreeing with the ambient end products: for some $\varepsilon>0$, its image near the lower end is $K_0\times[0,\varepsilon)$ and near the upper end is $K_1\times(1-\varepsilon,1]$. PL local-flatness means that each interior pair chart is PL-homeomorphic to $(\mathbb R^4,\mathbb R^2)$ and each boundary pair chart is PL-homeomorphic to $(\mathbb R^4_+,\mathbb R^2_+)$. Annuli with cone singularities or other non-locally-flat points are excluded. This definition makes no assertion identifying PL concordance with smooth or locally flat topological concordance.

before.title: A positive Hopf plumbing gives the trefoil Seifert matrix

before.statement:
Assume the full Axiom of Choice. A positive Hopf band is an oriented annulus whose two boundary components, with their induced orientations, have linking number $+1$. Let $F$ be the genus-one Seifert surface obtained by plumbing two positive Hopf bands in a square, with oriented core curves $a,b$ forming a positive handle basis, and choose the plumbing side so that $a^+$ bounds a disk in $S^3$ disjoint from $b$. The oriented boundary of this standard positive two-band plumbing is the right-handed trefoil. In the positive-push convention $V_{ij}=\operatorname{lk}(a_i^+,a_j)$ with ordered basis $(a,b)$, the Seifert matrix is
$$
V=\begin{pmatrix}-1&0\\-1&-1\end{pmatrix}.
$$

after.statement:
Assume the full Axiom of Choice. A positive Hopf band is an oriented annulus with unknotted core whose two boundary components, with their induced orientations, have linking number $+1$. Let $F$ be the genus-one Seifert surface obtained by plumbing two positive Hopf bands in a square, with oriented core curves $a,b$ forming a positive handle basis, and choose the plumbing side so that $a^+$ bounds a disk in $S^3$ disjoint from $b$. The oriented boundary of this standard positive two-band plumbing is the right-handed trefoil. In the positive-push convention $V_{ij}=\operatorname{lk}(a_i^+,a_j)$ with ordered basis $(a,b)$, the Seifert matrix is
$$
V=\begin{pmatrix}-1&0\\-1&-1\end{pmatrix}.
$$

More generally, the same matrix conclusion holds for any genus-one Seifert surface obtained by plumbing two oriented annuli with induced boundary linking number $+1$, provided their core curves form the stated positive handle basis and the stated disk for $a^+$ is disjoint from $b$. This broader matrix assertion does not identify the boundary knot.

before.title: Bounding-chain expression for a torsion linking pairing
before.statement: Let $Y$ be a closed oriented $3$-manifold and let $x,y\in\operatorname{Tor}H_1(Y;\mathbb Z)$. For choices of an integer $n>0$ and an integral $2$-chain $C$ with $\partial C=nx$, the bounding-chain expression is $(C\cdot y)/n\bmod\mathbb Z\in\mathbb Q/\mathbb Z$, where $C$ and $y$ are placed transversely and intersection signs use the orientation of $Y$. This expression is the torsion linking pairing when its independence of the choices is established.

before.title: Zero-framed surgery on a knot
before.statement: Assume countable choice as required by the chosen tubular-neighborhood and peripheral-system data. Let K be a smooth oriented knot with compact exterior E_K, positive meridian mu_K, and preferred longitude lambda_K on the boundary torus. The zero-framed surgery manifold M(K) is the closed oriented 3-manifold obtained by gluing D²×S¹ to E_K so that the meridian boundary circle of D²×{1} is identified with lambda_K and the core {0}×S¹ is identified with mu_K. The orientation extends the orientation of E_K across the filling. Thus the filling slope is the preferred zero-linking longitude; the definition asserts no 4-manifold bounded by M(K).

before.statement:
Let $M$ be a closed oriented three-manifold with a specified coefficient homomorphism $\phi:\pi_1(M_j)\to\Gamma$ on each component, where $\Gamma$ is PTFA. The integral coefficient ring is $\Lambda=\mathbb Z[\Gamma]$ with its fraction division ring $K\Gamma$. More generally let $k$ be $\mathbb Z$ or a commutative field, let $K$ be the fraction division ring of $k[\Gamma]$, and let $k[\Gamma]\subseteq R\subseteq K$ be an involution-stable unital intermediate ring. The involution fixes $k$ and sends $g$ to $g^{-1}$; on fractions it is the involutive anti-automorphism extending this formula. Taking $k=\mathbb Z$ and $R=\Lambda$ recovers the integral convention.

If $H_1(M;K)=0$, the coefficient Bockstein, oriented Poincaré duality and evaluation define the Blanchfield linking pairing
$$B_{M,\phi,R}:TH_1(M;R)\times TH_1(M;R)\longrightarrow K/R.$$
Here $T$ denotes the submodule of elements with a nonzero right annihilator, the first variable is conjugate-linear, and the second is right-linear. Nonsingularity means that the adjoint
$$\overline{TH_1(M;R)}\longrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}_R(TH_1(M;R),K/R)$$
is an isomorphism of left $R$-modules, where $r\cdot\bar x=\overline{x\bar r}$ on the conjugate module. This is equivalent to the conjugate-dual formulation in the right-module convention. For $\Gamma=\mathbb Z$ with generator $t$, $R=\mathbb Z[t^{\pm1}]$ and $K=\mathbb Q(t)$ give the classical coefficient convention. Nonsingularity is a separate property of the defined pairing, with its coefficient hypotheses supplied by the nonsingularity theorem.

For a homomorphism φ:π₁(M)→G and an extension ψ:π₁(W)→G over a compact oriented 4-manifold W with ∂W=M, define the signature defect by ρ(M,φ;W,ψ)=sign_G^(2)(W,ψ)−sign(W). It is an invariant of (M,φ) only when a separate bordism-independence theorem applies.

before.title: Signature additivity under gluing
before.statement:
Let W₀ and W₁ be compact oriented smooth 4-manifolds with a common identified boundary M, and let Γ be a discrete group. Suppose coefficient homomorphisms ψ_i:π₁(W_i)→Γ agree on π₁(M), and let X=W₀∪_M(−W₁) be the resulting closed oriented 4-manifold with its glued coefficient map. Then
sign(X)=sign(W₀)−sign(W₁)
and
sign_Γ^(2)(X)=sign_Γ^(2)(W₀,ψ₀)−sign_Γ^(2)(W₁,ψ₁).

$$H_1(M_{0,q};\mathbb Z)\cong H_1(\Sigma_q(K);\mathbb Z)\oplus\mathbb Z,$$

before.title: Torsion linking form and Casson–Gordon bordism data
before.statement: Assume AC. Let $K$ be a smooth oriented knot, $q\ge2$, and $M=\Sigma_q(K)$ oriented as the boundary of the positive-meridian branched cover. When $H_1(M;\mathbb Z)$ is finite, its torsion linking form is the oriented pairing $\lambda_M:H_1(M;\mathbb Z)\times H_1(M;\mathbb Z)\to\mathbb Q/\mathbb Z$ given by $\lambda_M(x,y)=(C\cdot y)/n\bmod\mathbb Z$ for any integer $n>0$ and integral $2$-chain $C$ in $M$ with $\partial C=nx$; reversing the orientation negates $\lambda_M$. For a prime-power-order character $\chi$ of order $d$, the standard splitting $H_1(M_{0,q};\mathbb Z)\cong H_1(M;\mathbb Z)\oplus\mathbb Z\langle\widetilde\mu\rangle$ of the $q$-fold cyclic cover $M_{0,q}$ of zero surgery extends $\chi$ to $\eta:H_1(M_{0,q};\mathbb Z)\to\mathbb Z/d\oplus\mathbb Z$ by identifying its cyclic image with $\mathbb Z/d$ and using the free-summand projection in the second factor. A Casson–Gordon bordism datum is a positive integer $r$ and a compact oriented $4$-manifold $W$ with a map to $K(\mathbb Z/d\oplus\mathbb Z,1)$ whose boundary represents $r$ copies of $(M_{0,q},\eta)$.
before.strategy: direct

after.statement: Assume AC. Let $K$ be a smooth oriented knot, $q\ge2$, and $M=\Sigma_q(K)$ oriented as the boundary of the positive-meridian branched cover. When $H_1(M;\mathbb Z)$ is finite, its torsion linking form is the oriented pairing $\lambda_M:H_1(M;\mathbb Z)\times H_1(M;\mathbb Z)\to\mathbb Q/\mathbb Z$ given by $\lambda_M(x,y)=(C\cdot b)/n\bmod\mathbb Z$, where integral $1$-cycles $a,b$ represent $x,y$, respectively, $n>0$ is an integer, and $C$ is an integral $2$-chain in $M$ with $\partial C=na$, placed transversely to $b$; reversing the orientation negates $\lambda_M$. For a prime-power-order character $\chi$ of order $d$, the standard splitting $H_1(M_{0,q};\mathbb Z)\cong H_1(M;\mathbb Z)\oplus\mathbb Z\langle\widetilde\mu\rangle$ of the $q$-fold cyclic cover $M_{0,q}$ of zero surgery extends $\chi$ to $\eta:H_1(M_{0,q};\mathbb Z)\to\mathbb Z/d\oplus\mathbb Z$ by identifying its cyclic image with $\mathbb Z/d$ and using the free-summand projection in the second factor. A Casson–Gordon bordism datum is a positive integer $r$ and a compact oriented $4$-manifold $W$ with a map to $K(\mathbb Z/d\oplus\mathbb Z,1)$ whose boundary represents $r$ copies of $(M_{0,q},\eta)$.
after.strategy: direct

before.statement: Let $X$ be a compact oriented topological $4$-manifold with nonempty boundary. A **kinky handle** is a standard $2$-handle whose core disk has finitely many transverse self-plumbings; a **framed Casson-handle tower** is a nested sequence of such stages in which each self-plumbing point of one stage is replaced by a framed kinky handle at the next stage, with the attaching regions matching the preceding stage. Suppose a finite family of these tower $4$-neighborhoods is embedded pairwise disjointly in $X$, with attaching circles in $\partial X$, and carries the algebraic dual data of a disk-embedding datum. If each embedded tower has a homeomorphism of pairs to the standard open $2$-handle $D^2\times\mathbb R^2$ that takes its specified framed attaching region, including its core circle and normal-framing class, to the standard attaching region $S^1\times\mathbb R^2$ with its standard framing, then the inverse images of the cores $D^2\times\{0\}$ form a pairwise disjoint family of locally flat properly embedded disks in $X$, with the prescribed framed boundary circles.

before.statement: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $X$ be a compact connected oriented smooth $4$-manifold with nonempty boundary and good fundamental group $G=\pi_1(X)$. Let $f_1,\ldots,f_n:(D^2,S^1)\looparrowright(X,\partial X)$ be proper generic immersed disks with pairwise disjoint embedded boundary circles. before.title: Index formula for the sign-fixed self-dual deformation operator
before.statement: Assume full AC. Let $X$ be a closed connected oriented smooth Riemannian four-manifold, let $b_1(X)=\dim H^1(X;\mathbb R)$, let $b_-(X)$ be the dimension of the negative subspace of its real intersection form, and let $P\to X$ be a smooth principal $SU(2)$-bundle. Put $k=-\langle c_2(P),[X]\rangle$. For the real Fredholm operator $D_A=d_A^*\oplus d_A^-$ from first Sobolev one-forms with values in $\operatorname{ad}P$ to zeroth Sobolev zero-forms and anti-self-dual two-forms, its Fredholm index is $8k-3(1-b_1(X)+b_-(X))$. In particular, if $\pi_1(X)=0$, the intersection form is positive definite, and $c_2(P)[X]=-1$, then $\operatorname{ind}_{\mathbb R}(D_A)=5$.

before.statement: Let P be a pattern and let K be a knot. Choose a transverse meridional disk for P and a short product slab about it. Form a pattern P_K by replacing all strands of P across that slab by parallel untwisted copies of a long-knot representative of K, with the individual strand orientations inherited from P; this is simultaneous companion insertion, rather than tying K into just one arc. For every knot J, the satellite P(K#J) is isotopic as an oriented knot to P_K(J). The pattern P_K has the same winding number as P.

before.title: Integral solvability and Blanchfield bordism for iterated infection

references.title: Jae Choon Cha and Taehee Kim, “Iterated satellite operators on the knot concordance group”
references.locator: §§4.1–4.3 and Appendix A, infection cobordism and Blanchfield bordism

before.statement:
Let $n\ge1$. Supply a compact connected oriented topological four-manifold $V$ with boundary a marked knot zero surgery, $H_1(V;\mathbb Z)=\mathbb Z$ and $H_2(V;\mathbb Z)=\mathbb Z^{2r}$, and exactly $r$ integral pairs $x_i,y_i\in H_2(V;\mathbb Z[\pi/\pi^{(n)}])$, $\pi=\pi_1(V)$, satisfying $\lambda(x_i,x_j)=0$ and $\lambda(x_i,y_j)=\delta_{ij}$. Form $W$ by any finite sequence of the actual marked standard connected-sum and winding-zero infection cobordism adjunctions along outgoing knot-surgery components, including orientation reversals, using supplied smooth peripheral products and collars. Let $\phi:\pi_1(W)\to\Gamma$ have PTFA target and restrict on $V$ through $\pi/\pi^{(n)}$. Take $k=\mathbb Q$ or $\mathbb F_p$ and put $A=k[\Gamma]$, with involutive Ore fraction division ring $K$ and the based standard parallel Hermitian structure.

The image pairs $\ell_i,d_i\in H_2(W;A)$ satisfy $\lambda(\ell_i,\ell_j)=0$ and $\lambda(\ell_i,d_j)=\lambda(d_j,\ell_i)=\delta_{ij}$. Their localized boundary-intersection cokernel has dimension at most $2r$. For each boundary component $M_0$ on which $\phi$ is nontrivial, $H_1(M_0;K)=0$, its coefficient Bockstein–duality linking form is defined, and its actual inclusion kernel is isotropic:
$$B_{M_0}(z,w)=0\quad\text{for all }z,w\in\ker\{H_1(M_0;A)\to H_1(W;A)\}.$$
Thus every boundary class with nonzero self-pairing survives in $H_1(W;A)$ and lies outside every isotropic submodule. If a component's coefficient image is cyclic, its form additionally has the nonsingularity furnished by the cyclic-image coefficient theorem; no unrestricted PTFA nonsingularity is asserted.

For a finite forest of iterated winding-zero infections with these initial data, suppose each top meridian generates $H_1(W_n;\mathbb Z)=\mathbb Z$ up to sign, and each pattern-axis integral classical self-pairing is nonzero. Use the actual intermediate $W_j$, rational mixed coefficients through index $n$, and one bottom field $\mathbb F_p$. For every odd prime outside the explicit finite exceptional set of the axis values, every branch meridian has a nonzero class in $P^{n-j}\pi_1(W_j)/P^{n-j+1}\pi_1(W_j)$, of infinite order when $j>0$ and order $p$ when $j=0$. All these conclusions hold for the supplied locally flat topological bordisms and smooth bordisms without a choice principle. Existence of the initial $V$ and its lifted pairs from a concordance relation is a separate hypothesis, as are analytic rho invariance and signature vanishing.

before.title: Compute the Kauffman polynomial from a BMW braid closure
before.statement:
**Input and output.** The input is one finite ASCII string. Its prescribed form is
`n;ell;word`, where `n` and `ell` are canonical decimal natural numbers
(`0`, or a nonzero decimal digit followed by zero or more decimal digits), and
`word` is empty if $\ell=0$ or is exactly $\ell$ comma-separated tokens of
the form `i+` or `i-`, with `i` a canonical decimal natural number. There is
no whitespace or trailing character. The output is either the rejection symbol
`REJECT` or an element of the coefficient extension $T$ with $a=\rho$ and
$d=\delta$.

1. **Parse and validate.** If the input is not in the stated syntax, if
   $\ell$ is not the number of letter tokens, if $n=0$, or if any token index
   fails $1\le i<n$, return `REJECT` and halt. Otherwise read the tokens as the
   finite signed Artin word
   $$\beta=\sigma_{i_1}^{\varepsilon_1}\cdots\sigma_{i_\ell}^{\varepsilon_\ell}, \qquad \varepsilon_j\in\{-1,1\}.$$

2. **Compute the closure data.** Form the BMW product
   $b_\beta=g_{i_1}^{\varepsilon_1}\cdots g_{i_\ell}^{\varepsilon_\ell}$.
   Set $w=\sum_{j=1}^{\ell}\varepsilon_j$ and let $c$ be the number of cycles,
   including fixed points, of the permutation $s_{i_1}\cdots s_{i_\ell}$ of
   $\{1,\ldots,n\}$.

3. **Enumerate a matching basis.** Work in the unit rectangle $R=[0,1]^2$ with top and
   bottom endpoints at $(j/(n+1),1)$ and $(j/(n+1),0)$, respectively, for
   $1\le j\le n$. Fix a prefix-free binary encoding of finite rational
   polygonal diagrams with over/under data, with rational coordinates written
   as reduced numerator/positive-denominator pairs. Number the tangle endpoints in cyclic order
   $1,2,\ldots,n,\bar n,\ldots,\bar2,\bar1$. Enumerate perfect matchings
   recursively: pair the least unmatched endpoint with each greater unmatched
   endpoint in increasing order, then continue on the remaining endpoints. For
   each matching $\mu$, scan finite diagram codes in increasing code length and
   then lexicographically. Choose the first code of a rational polygonal tangle
   diagram with that connector, no closed component and no strand self-crossing,
   in which the open strands are oriented from their lower-numbered to their
   higher-numbered endpoint, ordered by initial endpoint, and every crossing is
   over on the first traversed strand. This is the standard descending
   representative $T_\mu$. Give each polygonal segment its distinct code label
   and its orientation inherited from its strand. The spanning lemma identifies the standard descending class for each connector.

4. **Build generator matrices by skein reduction.** For every signed generator
   $g_i^{\pm1}$, form its left-multiplication matrix in the ordered basis
   $\{T_\mu\}$. The column at $T_\mu$ is computed by reducing
   $g_i^{\pm1}T_\mu$. In each current diagram, orient open strands from the smaller to the larger endpoint
   label and order them by their initial endpoints. Order closed components by
   their least segment labels. In each closed component, start by traversing its
   least-labelled segment from its designated initial endpoint to its terminal
   endpoint; then follow the unique continuation of that component, traversing
   later segments in whichever direction reaches the next endpoint. At a crossing
   continue along the same strand, and after a smoothing continue along the
   prescribed pairing. Retain segment labels and their designated endpoints
   through switches and smoothings. This gives a deterministic traversal even
   when segment orientations do not join coherently around a closed component.
   Traverse the open strands followed by the closed components in this order,
   and select the first crossing whose first encountered branch is under. Let $R(D)$ denote the
   coordinate vector of the current tangle expression in the matching basis.
   If the selected crossing is $D_+$ in the fixed chart, put $\eta=1$; if it
   is $D_-$, put $\eta=-1$. Replace
   $$R(D)=R(D^{\mathrm{sw}})+\eta z_D\bigl(R(D_0)-R(D_\infty)\bigr),$$
   using the fixed through smoothing $D_0$ and cup-cap smoothing $D_\infty$.
   Recurse on all three resulting terms. The switched branch has one fewer
   non-descending crossing and each smoothing has one fewer crossing. At a
   descending tangle leaf, use the traversal to lift each already traversed
   segment over the remaining diagram, removing self-crossings while fixing
   the boundary; retain crossings between distinct open strands in their
   ordered layers. Remove the resulting framing curls with factors $a$ or
   $a^{-1}$ and each closed component with factor $d$. Record the remaining
   standard matching tangle and add its coefficient to that matching coordinate.

5. **Apply the matrices and evaluate the trace row.** Start with the coordinate
   vector of the identity tangle and apply the generator matrices from the
   rightmost braid letter to the leftmost, obtaining $v_\beta$, the coordinate
   vector of $\Phi_n(b_\beta)$. For each matching $\mu$, close $T_\mu$ by the following fixed untwisted
   planar closure. For $1\le j\le n$ put $x_j=j/(n+1)$ and
   $\epsilon_j=1/(j+1)$, and add the rational polygonal arc

   $$C_j:(x_j,1)\to(x_j,1+\epsilon_j)\to(1+\epsilon_j,1+\epsilon_j)\to(1+\epsilon_j,-\epsilon_j)\to(x_j,-\epsilon_j)\to(x_j,0).$$

   These arcs lie outside $R$ except at their specified endpoints and are
   pairwise disjoint: if $j<k$, then $x_j<x_k$ and $\epsilon_j>\epsilon_k$,
   so their exterior lanes are nested. Orient $C_j$ from top endpoint $j$ to
   bottom endpoint $\bar j$, give its segments fresh distinct labels, and use
   this same arc system for every matching. It represents the untwisted closure
   used in the definition of $\tau_n$. Evaluate the closed diagram by the
   deterministic traversal and skein recursion of Step 4: at a descending leaf,
   straighten the traversal-ordered components, remove their framing curls with
   factors $a,a^{-1}$, remove each free circle with factor $d$, and use
   $P(\varnothing)=1$ for the empty diagram.

   Set
   $$t_\mu=d^{-n}P(\widehat{T_\mu}),\qquad \tau_n(b_\beta)=t^{\mathsf T}v_\beta.$$

6. **Return**
   $$-(-1)^c a^{-w}d^{n-1}\tau_n(b_\beta).$$

after.title: Compute the Kauffman polynomial from a BMW braid closure
after.statement:
**Input and output.** The input is one finite ASCII string. Its prescribed form is
`n;ell;word`, where `n` and `ell` are canonical decimal natural numbers
(`0`, or a nonzero decimal digit followed by zero or more decimal digits), and
`word` is empty if $\ell=0$ or is exactly $\ell$ comma-separated tokens of
the form `i+` or `i-`, with `i` a canonical decimal natural number. There is
no whitespace or trailing character. The output is either the rejection symbol
`REJECT` or an element of the converted coefficient ring
$$T_K=\mathbb Z[i,A^{\pm1},Z,d^{\pm1},q^{\pm1}]/(i^2+1,\ Z(d-1)+A+A^{-1},\ q-q^{-1}-iZ).$$
Steps 2–5 use the Dubrovnik coefficient extension $T$, with $a=\rho$ and
$d=\delta$; Step 6 uses the ring homomorphism
$$\varphi:T\longrightarrow T_K,\qquad (a,z,d,q)\longmapsto(-iA,iZ,d,q).$$

1. **Parse and validate.** If the input is not in the stated syntax, if
   $\ell$ is not the number of letter tokens, if $n=0$, or if any token index
   fails $1\le i<n$, return `REJECT` and halt. Otherwise read the tokens as the
   finite signed Artin word
   $$\beta=\sigma_{i_1}^{\varepsilon_1}\cdots\sigma_{i_\ell}^{\varepsilon_\ell}, \qquad \varepsilon_j\in\{-1,1\}.$$

2. **Compute the closure data.** Form the BMW product
   $b_\beta=g_{i_1}^{\varepsilon_1}\cdots g_{i_\ell}^{\varepsilon_\ell}$.
   Set $w=\sum_{j=1}^{\ell}\varepsilon_j$ and let $c$ be the number of cycles,
   including fixed points, of the permutation $s_{i_1}\cdots s_{i_\ell}$ of
   $\{1,\ldots,n\}$.

3. **Enumerate a matching basis.** Work in the unit rectangle $R=[0,1]^2$ with top and
   bottom endpoints at $(j/(n+1),1)$ and $(j/(n+1),0)$, respectively, for
   $1\le j\le n$. Fix a prefix-free binary encoding of finite rational
   polygonal diagrams with over/under data, with rational coordinates written
   as reduced numerator/positive-denominator pairs. Number the tangle endpoints in cyclic order
   $1,2,\ldots,n,\bar n,\ldots,\bar2,\bar1$. Enumerate perfect matchings
   recursively: pair the least unmatched endpoint with each greater unmatched
   endpoint in increasing order, then continue on the remaining endpoints. For
   each matching $\mu$, scan finite diagram codes in increasing code length and
   then lexicographically. Choose the first code of a rational polygonal tangle
   diagram with that connector, no closed component and no strand self-crossing,
   in which the open strands are oriented from their lower-numbered to their
   higher-numbered endpoint, ordered by initial endpoint, and every crossing is
   over on the first traversed strand. This is the standard descending
   representative $T_\mu$. Give each polygonal segment its distinct code label
   and its orientation inherited from its strand. The spanning lemma identifies the standard descending class for each connector.

4. **Build generator matrices by skein reduction.** For every signed generator
   $g_i^{\pm1}$, form its left-multiplication matrix in the ordered basis
   $\{T_\mu\}$. The column at $T_\mu$ is computed by reducing
   $g_i^{\pm1}T_\mu$. For each initial reducer input (a matrix column here or a
   closed trace diagram in Step 5), first fix pairwise disjoint rational crossing
   boxes, each meeting only its two crossing branches, in four boundary ports,
   and containing no polygonal vertex. Choose the first admissible finite tuple
   in the length-then-lexicographic rational coding order of Step 3. Make the
   boxes small enough that every component contains a segment portion outside
   the boxes. Subdivide all polygonal segments at their box-boundary ports.
   Give the portions outside the boxes fresh distinct labels in their finite
   diagram-code order; designate the lexicographically smaller coordinate
   endpoint of each portion as its initial endpoint. Retain these portions,
   labels, and endpoints throughout that reduction tree. Inside each box record
   either the original crossing pairing or one of its two smoothing pairings;
   switches change only over/under data, and smoothings change only this pairing.
   In each current diagram, orient open strands from the smaller to the larger
   boundary endpoint label and order them by their initial endpoints. Order
   closed components by their least portion labels. Start each closed component
   along its least-labelled portion from its designated initial endpoint to its
   other endpoint, then follow its unique continuation. Inside a crossing box
   follow its current pairing. No portion is split or relabelled by a switch or
   smoothing, and every resulting component contains a labelled portion. This
   determines the traversal even when the designated directions of successive
   portions disagree.
   Traverse the open strands followed by the closed components in this order,
   and select the first crossing whose first encountered branch is under. Let $R(D)$ denote the
   coordinate vector of the current tangle expression in the matching basis.
   If the selected crossing is $D_+$ in the fixed chart, put $\eta=1$; if it
   is $D_-$, put $\eta=-1$. Replace
   $$R(D)=R(D^{\mathrm{sw}})+\eta z_D\bigl(R(D_0)-R(D_\infty)\bigr),$$
   using the fixed through smoothing $D_0$ and cup-cap smoothing $D_\infty$.
   Recurse on all three resulting terms. The switched branch has one fewer
   non-descending crossing and each smoothing has one fewer crossing. At a
   descending tangle leaf, use the traversal to lift each already traversed
   segment over the remaining diagram, removing self-crossings while fixing
   the boundary; retain crossings between distinct open strands in their
   ordered layers. Remove the resulting framing curls with factors $a$ or
   $a^{-1}$ and each closed component with factor $d$. Record the remaining
   standard matching tangle and add its coefficient to that matching coordinate.

5. **Apply the matrices and evaluate the trace row.** Start with the coordinate
   vector of the identity tangle and apply the generator matrices from the
   rightmost braid letter to the leftmost, obtaining $v_\beta$, the coordinate
   vector of $\Phi_n(b_\beta)$. For each matching $\mu$, close $T_\mu$ by the following fixed untwisted
   planar closure. For $1\le j\le n$ put $x_j=j/(n+1)$ and
   $\epsilon_j=1/(j+1)$, and add the rational polygonal arc

   $$C_j:(x_j,1)\to(x_j,1+\epsilon_j)\to(1+\epsilon_j,1+\epsilon_j)\to(1+\epsilon_j,-\epsilon_j)\to(x_j,-\epsilon_j)\to(x_j,0).$$

   These arcs lie outside $R$ except at their specified endpoints and are
   pairwise disjoint: if $j<k$, then $x_j<x_k$ and $\epsilon_j>\epsilon_k$,
   so their exterior lanes are nested. Orient $C_j$ from top endpoint $j$ to
   bottom endpoint $\bar j$, give its segments fresh distinct labels, and use
   this same arc system for every matching. It represents the untwisted closure
   used in the definition of $\tau_n$. Evaluate the closed diagram by the
   deterministic traversal and skein recursion of Step 4: at a descending leaf,
   straighten the traversal-ordered components, remove their framing curls with
   factors $a,a^{-1}$, remove each free circle with factor $d$, and use
   $P(\varnothing)=1$ for the empty diagram.

   Set
   $$t_\mu=d^{-n}P(\widehat{T_\mu}),\qquad \tau_n(b_\beta)=t^{\mathsf T}v_\beta.$$

6. **Convert parameters and return.** Substitute $a=-iA$ and $z=iZ$ in
   the expression $d^{n-1}\tau_n(b_\beta)$ computed in Step 5, leaving $d,q$
   fixed and interpreting all coefficients in $T_K$. Return
   $$-i^w(-1)^c A^{-w}\varphi\!\left(d^{n-1}\tau_n(b_\beta)\right).$$

before.title: The BMW braid-closure algorithm terminates and returns its stated value
before.statement:
For every finite ASCII input string, the BMW braid-closure algorithm parses the
form `n;ell;word`, where `n` and `ell` are canonical decimal natural numbers
(`0`, or a nonzero decimal digit followed by zero or more decimal digits), and
`word` is empty if $\ell=0$ or is exactly $\ell$ comma-separated tokens of the
form `i+` or `i-`, with `i` a canonical decimal natural number. There is no
whitespace or trailing character. It returns `REJECT` exactly when the string
fails this syntax, the parsed value of $\ell$ differs from the actual number of
letter tokens, the parsed strand count is $n=0$, or some letter index fails
$1\le i<n$. For every other input, the algorithm terminates after finitely
many basis-code searches, algebra operations, and skein reductions, and returns exactly
$$-(-1)^c a^{-w}d^{n-1}\tau_n(\beta).$$
Here $w$ is the determinant writhe of the oriented closure, $c$ is its
component count, and $\tau_n$ is the normalized scalar closure trace. No
asymptotic complexity bound is asserted.

before.title: The Kauffman and Dubrovnik polynomials agree under the stated conversion
before.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $K$ be a nonempty oriented link with determinant writhe $w(K)$ and component count $c(K)$, and let $Q_K$ be the value returned by the BMW braid-closure algorithm for any finite signed braid word representing $K$. Then $Q_K$ is independent of the chosen braid and
$$Q_K=F_K(ia,-iz)=-(-1)^{c(K)}a^{-w(K)}D_K(a,z),$$
equivalently,
$$D_K(a,z)=-i^{-w(K)}(-1)^{c(K)}L_K(ia,-iz),\qquad i^2=-1.$$
The proof covers the unknot, positive and negative curls, and both self-crossing split and mixed-crossing merge smoothing cases under the stated universal coefficient relation, without dividing by $z$.

after.title: The Kauffman and Dubrovnik polynomials agree under the stated conversion
after.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Fix any nonempty oriented regular link diagram $K$, with determinant writhe $w(K)$ and component count $c(K)$. Let $Q_K(A,Z)\in T_K$ denote the value returned by the BMW braid-closure algorithm for any finite signed braid word whose closure represents the oriented link represented by $K$. The quantities $D_K$ and $L_K$ below are evaluated on this fixed diagram; $F_K$ and $Q_K$ depend only on its ambient oriented link type. Then $Q_K$ is independent of the chosen braid and
$$Q_K(A,Z)=F_K(A,Z)=-i^{w(K)}(-1)^{c(K)}A^{-w(K)}D_K(-iA,iZ),$$
with the inverse conversion
$$D_K(a,z)=-i^{-w(K)}(-1)^{c(K)}L_K(ia,-iz),\qquad i^2=-1.$$
The proof covers the unknot, positive and negative curls, and both self-crossing split and mixed-crossing merge smoothing cases under the stated universal coefficient relation, without dividing by $z$.

before.title: BMW Kauffman and Dubrovnik worked cases
before.statement: For the one-component unknot, the Dubrovnik value and the normalized Kauffman value are both $1$. Adding a positive or negative curl multiplies the regular-isotopy Dubrovnik value by $a$ or $a^{-1}$, while the writhe correction leaves the ambient Kauffman value unchanged. For the two-component unlink, the Dubrovnik value is $d$, the identity $2$-braid closure has normalized trace $1$, and the BMW algorithm returns the Kauffman value $-d$. These calculations hold in the universal coefficient ring with $z(d-1)=a-a^{-1}$ and do not invert $z$.

before.statement:
Assume full AC for the surgery-presentation and universal-construction inputs below. Fix an even integer $p\ge4$, a primitive $2p$-th root $A\in\mathbb C$, put $r=p/2$ and $\delta=-A^2-A^{-2}$, and use the selected BHMV sixth root $\kappa$ satisfying $\kappa^6=A^{-6-(p+1)p/2}$. Fix a closed oriented marked surface $\Sigma$ with its Lagrangian and weighted anomaly data. before.title: Ribbon evaluation from a colored braid word
before.statement:
An **effective field** is a field whose elements have finite encodings and whose exact addition, subtraction, multiplication, equality test, and inversion of nonzero elements are terminating procedures. Input a finite-dimensional strict matrix realization of a $k$-linear ribbon category with $\operatorname{End}(\mathbf1)=k$, finite-dimensional color objects with fixed bases, exact matrices for every braiding and inverse braiding used, the evaluation and coevaluation maps for the closure, the twist matrices, and the matrix $J_W$ of the ribbon-induced pivotal comparison $j_W=u_W\circ\theta_W:W\to W^{\vee\vee}$ for $W=V_{a_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes V_{a_n}$, where $u_W$ is the Drinfeld morphism. Also input a finite braid word $\beta$ on $n\ge1$ strands and the top color tuple $(a_1,\ldots,a_n)$. The matrices are assumed to satisfy the stated ribbon-category axioms; an implementation does not infer those axioms from arbitrary matrices.

Use the strand-position permutation homomorphism $\pi:B_n\to\operatorname{Sym}(\{1,\ldots,n\})$ given by $\pi(\sigma_i)=(i\ i+1)$. Read the braid letters in composition order, updating the current color tuple at each crossing by swapping its adjacent colors. For a positive letter $\sigma_i$, use the matrix of
$$1\otimes\cdots\otimes c_{V_{a_i},V_{a_{i+1}}}\otimes\cdots\otimes1,$$
and for a negative letter use its inverse. Let the blackboard-framed closure join the bottom and top endpoint at each position by the identity pairing. Reject the input if the final color tuple differs from the initial tuple: the tuple records the colors at the paired endpoints, so equality is exactly the condition that the closure carries a consistent color on every component. Starting with the identity matrix, multiply the typed crossing matrices in word order to obtain $M_\beta:W\to W$, then return the finite matrix contraction
$$\operatorname{ev}_{W^\vee}\bigl((J_WM_\beta)\otimes1_{W^\vee}\bigr)\operatorname{coev}_W\in k.$$
In ordinary dual-basis coordinates this contraction is the matrix trace $\operatorname{Tr}(J_WM_\beta)$.
This is the exact ribbon evaluation of the blackboard-framed colored braid closure in the given matrix realization. No algorithm is asserted for arbitrary abstract ribbon categories without effective finite matrix data.
before.strategy: Checks color preservation around permutation cycles, multiplies the typed positive or inverse braiding matrices in word order, and contracts the resulting endomorphism with the supplied pivotal trace matrices.

before.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $k$ be a field and let $\mathcal C$ be a $k$-linear ribbon category with $k$-bilinear tensor product and $\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal C}(\mathbf1)=k$. Let $X$ be absolutely simple, so its twist is $\theta_X=\lambda\operatorname{id}_X$ for a unique $\lambda\in k^\times$. For $n\ge1$ and $\beta\in B_n$, let $t_n(\beta)$ be the value of the blackboard-framed $X$-colored closure and let $w(\beta)$ be the exponent sum, with positive Artin generator and positive stabilization conventions fixed as in the supplied ribbon-trace formulas. Then
$$J_X(\widehat\beta):=\lambda^{-w(\beta)}t_n(\beta)$$
depends only on the oriented unframed link type of $\widehat\beta$ when every component has color $X$. This statement makes no normalization by the categorical dimension.

before.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. before.statement:
Fix the round metric and orientation on $S^3$. An **$m$-singular oriented knot** is a smooth immersion $K:S^1\to S^3$ with exactly $m$ distinct transverse double points and no other self-intersections; each double-point image has exactly two preimages with linearly independent tangent vectors, and the preimage pairs are disjoint. The knot has no framing. Choose disjoint small balls around its double points, each containing no other part of the singular knot. At each double point there are two **resolutions**, obtained by separating the two local branches in the ball; label them $+$ and $-$ so the resolved crossing signs are respectively $+1$ and $-1$ under the convention that, in a diagram whose positive viewing normal agrees with the ambient orientation, the sign is $\operatorname{sgn}\det(v_{\mathrm{over}},v_{\mathrm{under}})$ and the positive Artin half twist has sign $+1$.

A **framed oriented knot** is a smooth oriented embedding $K:S^1\hookrightarrow S^3$ together with a homotopy class through nowhere-zero smooth sections of its oriented rank-two normal bundle. For an immersion $K:S^1\to S^3$, including one with double points, define its branchwise normal bundle over the parameter circle by $\nu_K:=K^*TS^3/dK(TS^1)$, oriented so that a positive tangent followed by a positive normal basis gives the ambient orientation. Because $dK$ has rank one at every parameter, its image is locally a smooth line subbundle and this quotient is locally a rank-two bundle. A simple zero is one at which the derivative of the section in an oriented local trivialization is nonzero. Resolve double points as above, extending the normal section over the local resolution balls; each resulting section determines a framing homotopy class. To resolve a framing zero at parameter $t=0$, choose the oriented normal trivialization so the section is $t e_1$ near $0$, with $e_2$ the positive quarter-turn of $e_1$; replace it by $t e_1+\delta e_2$ or $t e_1-\delta e_2$ for sufficiently small $\delta>0$. where $K_\epsilon$ resolves singularity $i$ positively when $\epsilon_i=+1$ and negatively when $\epsilon_i=-1$. For $m=0$, set $D_0V(K)=V(K)$. before.statement:
For each finite degree cutoff $N$, every parenthesized endpoint cluster of the KZ connection has a unique coefficientwise tangentially regularized transport, obtained by removing its local residue factor. For three strands, fix the normalized positions $(0,z,1)$ and put $a=t_{12}/(2\pi i)$ and $b=t_{23}/(2\pi i)$. The equation $G'(z)=\left(\frac{a}{z}+\frac{b}{z-1}\right)G(z)$ has unique solutions $G_0,G_1$ with $G_0(z)=f(z)z^a$, $G_1(z)=g(1-z)(1-z)^b$, where $f$ and $g$ are analytic near $0$ and $f(0)=g(0)=1$. Their ratio $\Phi_{\mathrm{KZ}}:=G_1(z)^{-1}G_0(z)$ is independent of $z$ and equals the regularized limit $\Phi_{\mathrm{KZ}}=\lim_{\varepsilon\downarrow0}\varepsilon^{-b}G_\varepsilon(1-\varepsilon)\varepsilon^a,\qquad G_\varepsilon(\varepsilon)=1$.
If $K^+$ is obtained from a strict Morse knot presentation $K$ by inserting one copy of the fixed standard hump $H$, model the local birth by cutting the knot to a one-in one-out tangle $T_K$, composing with the standard one-in one-out hump tangle whose closure is $H$, and closing the composite. Then $Z(K^+)=Z(H)Z(K)$, $r(K^+)=r(K)+1$, and hence $I(K^+)=I(K)$. The inverse in $I(K)$ exists degreewise because the degree-zero coefficient of $Z(H)$ is $1$. The associator identities and independence under arbitrary changes of parenthesization are separate claims.

before.title: Finite-type truncations of the Kontsevich integral

references.title: Introduction to Vassiliev Knot Invariants, §8.8.1
The Fundamental Theorem of Vassiliev Invariants, §2.6

before.statement: Assume countable choice, and let $I_m(K)$ be the degree-$m$ homogeneous coefficient of the normalized unframed Kontsevich series $I(K)$ of a smooth oriented knot type $K$. For $n\ge0$, put $I_{\le n}(K)=\sum_{m=0}^{n}I_m(K)$. A function on knot types is of type at most $n$ when its alternating resolution sum on every $(n+1)$-singular knot is zero. Then $I_{\le n}$ is a type-at-most-$n$ invariant with values in the sum of the unframed degree-$m$ chord-diagram modules for $0\le m\le n$. For every $n$-singular knot with chord diagram $D$, its $n$-fold finite difference satisfies $D_n I_{\le n}(K)=D$. In particular, the degree-$n$ symbol is the identity on rational chord diagrams after extending scalars to $\mathbb C$; no rational-coefficient claim is made about $I_m(K)$.

before.title: Finite colored Jones evaluation is exact and representative-independent
before.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice and the prescribed generic matrix ribbon data for the $N$-dimensional color, where $N\ge1$. For every finite braid word $\beta$ on $n\ge1$ strands whose closure is a knot, the algorithm performs finitely many exact operations, including exactly one crossing-matrix update per letter and one finite pivotal-trace contraction, and returns the generic normalized value $J_N^{\mathrm{gen}}(\widehat\beta;q)$. If two such braid words close to the same oriented unframed knot, their returned generic values agree. The unique Laurent representative belongs to $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$, and its evaluation at any nonzero complex $q$ is defined, including at $q_N=e^{2\pi i/N}$.

before.title: Khovanov complexes are chain homotopy equivalent under Reidemeister moves
before.statement: Let $D,D'$ be finite regular oriented link diagrams related by a planar isotopy or one oriented Reidemeister move. Let $\bar C(D)$ be the integral signed state cube before the writhe shifts, with cohomological degree $|v|$ and quantum degree $|v|+\sum\deg(a)$, and normalize it by $C(D)=\bar C(D)[n_-]\{2n_--n_+\}$ to obtain the state degrees $i=|v|-n_-$ and $j=|v|+n_+-2n_-+\sum\deg(a)$. Before normalization, a positive type-I curl gives $\bar C(D_+)\simeq\bar C(D)\{1\}$, a negative type-I curl gives $\bar C(D_-)\simeq\bar C(D)[-1]\{-2\}$, a type-II move gives $\bar C(D_{II})\simeq\bar C(D)[-1]\{-1\}$, and a type-III move gives an unshifted equivalence. Consequently the normalized complexes are bigraded chain homotopy equivalent. If $D,D'$ are based knot diagrams and the move disk is disjoint from the basepoint, the same chain homotopy equivalence descends to their reduced quotient complexes, equivalently to the cut-tangle complexes with interval module $M=\mathbb Z$, $X\cdot1=0$.

before.title: Khovanov Euler characteristics equal the Jones polynomial
before.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $V_L(t)$ be the library Jones polynomial of a nonempty oriented link $L$, normalized by $V_{\bigcirc}(t)=1$. For every diagram $D$ of $L$, put $q=-A^{-2}$ and $t=q^2=A^{-4}$. Then the integral rank Euler characteristics satisfy
$$\sum_{i,j}(-1)^i\operatorname{rank}_{\mathbb Z}Kh^{i,j}(L)q^j=(q+q^{-1})V_L(t).$$
If $L=K$ is a knot with any basepoint $p$ away from the crossings, then
$$\sum_{i,\widetilde j}(-1)^i\operatorname{rank}_{\mathbb Z}\widetilde{Kh}^{i,\widetilde j}(K,p)q^{\widetilde j}=V_K(t).$$
The unreduced factor $q+q^{-1}$ and reduced factor $1$ are the respective unknot normalizations.

before.statement: Let a finite planar resolution cube be equipped with an arrow at each crossing, transported to its saddle edges while resolving the other disjoint crossing disks, and use the odd exterior merge and split maps. There is a function assigning a sign to every edge such that the resulting signed differential squares to zero over the integers. More precisely, one can prescribe the face products on all faces, including faces whose two composites vanish, as follows. On a face with nonzero composites let $\kappa\in\{1,-1\}$ be their relative commutation sign. On a zero-composite face the two saddle arcs have alternating endpoints on one circle, one arc inside and one outside; put them in the standard two-chord picture by an orientation-preserving planar isotopy and rotate so that the inside arrow points upwards and set $\kappa=1$ when the outside arrow points left, and $\kappa=-1$ when it points right. Then the prescribed product of the four edge signs is $-\kappa$. These prescriptions are consistent, and two edge assignments realizing the same prescriptions are related by a vertexwise sign change. All the constructions are finite and choice-free. The vertexwise comparison commutes with the marked right $\mathbb Z[X]/(X^2)$-action.

A smooth oriented knot cobordism from $K_0$ to $K_1$ is a compact smooth properly embedded oriented surface $\Sigma\subset S^3\times[0,1]$ whose boundary is $(-K_0\times\{0\})\sqcup(K_1\times\{1\})$, with product collars at both ends. A **generic movie** for $\Sigma$ is obtained by choosing a generic projection of the slices $S^3\times\{t\}$ to the plane and a Morse height function on $\Sigma$, then recording the oriented link diagram at each regular level. Intermediate regular levels may be links with any finite number of components. After choosing the projection and height generically, the finitely many exceptional levels are isolated and distinct: between them the diagrams change by planar isotopy or one oriented Reidemeister move, and at them the surface height has one nondegenerate minimum (a birth), one nondegenerate maximum (a death), or one index-one critical point (a saddle band move). A movie includes its ordered list of frames and these elementary changes; no claim that two movies of the same cobordism are equivalent is part of this definition.

references.title: Ozsváth and Szabó, Holomorphic disks and topological invariants for closed three-manifolds, §§2–3
Lipshitz, Heegaard Floer Homologies, §§2–5

before.statement:
Let $Y$ be a closed connected oriented smooth three-manifold. A pointed genus-$g$ Heegaard diagram for $Y$ consists of an embedded splitting $Y=U_\alpha\cup_\Sigma U_\beta$, where $\Sigma=\partial U_\alpha$ is a closed oriented genus-$g$ surface and each $U$ is a handlebody, meaning a regular neighborhood of a finite connected graph; ordered systems $\boldsymbol\alpha=(\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_g)$ and $\boldsymbol\beta=(\beta_1,\ldots,\beta_g)$ of pairwise disjoint smooth simple closed curves bounding specified disjoint proper compression disks in the respective handlebodies, each disk system cutting its handlebody into one ball; and one point $z$ off the curves. Opposite-system curves meet transversely in finitely many points. This is closed-manifold data; it includes neither a knot nor a second marked point.

Write $q:\Sigma^g\to\operatorname{Sym}^g(\Sigma)=\Sigma^g/S_g$ for the permutation quotient. The product tori are the images
$$T_\alpha=q(\alpha_1\times\cdots\times\alpha_g),\qquad T_\beta=q(\beta_1\times\cdots\times\beta_g).$$
The group $S_g$ acts on the ambient product, rather than on a fixed ordered product of distinct attaching circles. A generator is an intersection $x\in T_\alpha\cap T_\beta$; equivalently it selects one intersection point on each curve of each system. There are finitely many generators. For $g=0$ the symmetric product and both empty products are one point, with the empty generator.

A Whitney class $\phi\in\pi_2(x,y)$ is a relative homotopy class of maps of a closed disk with two marked boundary points into the symmetric product, taking its two boundary arcs into $T_\alpha,T_\beta$ and its marked points to $x,y$. Its domain is the integral two-chain of complementary regions; its coefficient at an interior point $p$ is the intersection multiplicity $n_p(\phi)$ with $\{p\}+\operatorname{Sym}^{g-1}(\Sigma)$. In particular $n_z(\phi)$ is the basepoint coefficient. A periodic domain is an integral region two-chain whose boundary is an integral sum of full attaching circles. The domain of a class $\psi\in\pi_2(x,x)$ is periodic. Such a class is normalized when $n_z(\psi)=0$. Write $\mu(\phi)$ for the real Fredholm index of the disk linearization, before quotienting longitudinal translation; well-definedness and its topological index formula are properties to be proved in the analytic and index theory.

For a periodic domain P, cap its full attaching-circle boundary with the specified compression disks, using the boundary multiplicities and orientations, to obtain the integral class $H(P)\in H_2(Y;\mathbb Z)$. A Spin-c structure $\mathfrak s$ is a lift of the oriented tangent frame bundle through $\operatorname{Spin}^c(3)\to SO(3)$; $c_1(\mathfrak s)$ is the first Chern class of its determinant line, with determinant character $[s,u]\mapsto u^2$. **Weak admissibility in the specified Spin-c sector $\mathfrak s$** means that EVERY nonzero integral periodic domain P with $n_z(P)=0$ and $\langle c_1(\mathfrak s),H(P)\rangle=0$ has both positive and negative region coefficients. This condition is imposed even when the sector has no diagram generators. It is a condition on domains and the intended sector, not only on periodic classes based at existing generators.

The ordinary sector module $\widehat{CF}(\mathcal H,\mathfrak s)$ uses generators with Morse Spin-c label $\mathfrak s_z(x)=\mathfrak s$. The label is defined by compatible handle Morse data: replace the gradient in disjoint tubes around the generator's index-one/index-two trajectories and the basepoint's index-zero/index-three trajectory by nonsingular fields, and take the Spin-c lift of their oriented perpendicular planes. Its actual construction, independence properties and periodic-index formula are obligations of the Spin-c and index theory. In particular the equality between the index of a REALIZED normalized periodic class based at x and the Chern evaluation in $\mathfrak s_z(x)$ is not assumed as its own proof. A realized-generator test alone is not substituted for the stated domain condition.

An **admissible diagram for the full single-diagram hat module** satisfies this sector condition for EVERY Spin-c structure on Y, including the sectors with no generators. The full module below uses all generators and hence all intended sectors; an empty sector contributes a zero summand but is not omitted from the admissibility test. Equivalently this full-diagram condition is global weak admissibility: every nonzero periodic domain with $n_z=0$ has both signs. The equivalence uses the actual zero-Chern Spin-c sector constructed from complete Heegaard data in Complete Heegaard data have a zero-Chern Spin-c sector; it is not inferred from a generator existing in that sector. For a SINGLE specified sector, ordinary weak admissibility remains the stated Chern-kernel condition and need not imply global weakness. No assertion of the full group from a diagram tested only at its represented sectors is made.

For $g>0$ choose a complex structure $j$ and positive area form on $\Sigma$. Analytic data include a smooth path $J_t$ on the symmetric product, constant on actual neighborhoods of $t=0,1$. On a fixed neighborhood of the diagonal and the point-divisors for a chosen interior point of every complementary region, including $z$, it agrees with the integrable structure $\operatorname{Sym}^g(j)$; away from that neighborhood it is tame for the form descended from the product surface area form. The path is chosen in a sufficiently small nearly symmetric class. Product-integrable normal forms near the finitely many transverse generators may be included among its specified auxiliary choices. Existence of such choices and of the regular perturbations needed below remains a mathematical obligation. A holomorphic strip is an actual smooth finite-Dirichlet-energy map $u:\mathbb R\times[0,1]\to\operatorname{Sym}^g(\Sigma)$ satisfying
$$u_s+J_t(u)u_t=0,\qquad u(s,0)\in T_\alpha,\quad u(s,1)\in T_\beta,$$
with uniform generator limits at both longitudinal ends. The space in class $\phi$ is $\mathcal M_J(\phi)$, and translation in $s$ acts on it. Regular means that its actual linearized operator is surjective at the solutions being counted. Local multiplicity positivity, Fredholmness, the class index and compactness are results to be proved, not choices of which maps to count.

The hat diagram-level module $\widehat{CF}(\mathcal H;\mathbb F_2)$ is free over $\mathbb F_2$ on the generators. For regular data for which the displayed quotient sets are finite and, for each $x$, only finitely many nonempty pairs $(y,\phi)$ occur, its candidate count operator is
$$\widehat\partial x=\sum_y\ \sum_{\substack{\phi\in\pi_2(x,y)\\\mu(\phi)=1,\ n_z(\phi)=0}}\#_2\bigl(\mathcal M_J(\phi)/\mathbb R\bigr)y.$$
Here $\#_2$ is parity of an actual finite zero-dimensional quotient. For $g=0$ the operator is zero on the empty generator. That the required regular finite counts exist, that $\widehat\partial^2=0$, and that its homology is invariant under changing pointed admissible diagrams and auxiliary choices are separate analytic and move theorems. Once these hold, the common homology is denoted $\widehat{HF}(Y;\mathbb F_2)$. No filtered chain-homotopy invariant, integral orientations or absolute grading is asserted by this definition.

Comparisons of embedded diagrams permit orientation-preserving isomorphisms carrying $Y$, its two handlebodies, their oriented surface, the attaching systems and $z$ to the specified counterparts, equivalently compatible collared extensions of the surface map. Curve-factor reordering gives the corresponding product identification. Analytic data are transported by the induced symmetric-product map, including $j$, the area form, protected neighborhoods and $J_t$. The intended count identification is the actual pushforward of generators and disk classes with these transported data; its compatibility with the operator requires proof. An ambient isotopy is not assumed to act as the identity. Comparison of independently chosen perturbations likewise requires the continuation theorem.

before.axiom_use: Assumes ACω for the explicit separable-Hilbert generic choices and countable compactness arguments in the proved suppliers; no full-AC transversality or Spin-c classification theorem is imported.
before.statement:
Assume ACω. Let a finite pointed Heegaard multidiagram have actual complete handlebody disk systems for closed oriented three-manifolds, with a basepoint in every one-system cut component. Ordered polygons use distinct labeled, pairwise transverse attaching systems; when an operation repeats a geometric system, use its separately labeled small transverse auxiliary copies. For the full hat operations impose global weak multidiagram admissibility: every nonzero full-curve multiperiodic domain vanishing at all basepoints has both signs. For operations in a specified total Spin-c family, ordinary weak admissibility is also allowed: every nonzero formal periodic domain difference in the capped Spin-c kernel, normalized at every mark and with Chern evaluation zero, has both signs. The same formal sector condition is imposed on each relevant boundary pair, including intended sectors with no generators. In this ordinary weak branch all basepoint multiplicities are fixed to zero, the required arities and compact auxiliary parameter families are finite, and counts use the corresponding fixed actual index bands. Strict all-mark normalized strong admissibility is a further allowed branch; it is not substituted for ordinary weakness. For a single diagram the full-module admissibility convention tests all intended Spin-c sectors, including empty sectors, and implies the required global weak domain condition.

In positive symmetric rank choose, among the auxiliary data, an arbitrarily small pointed Hamiltonian representative with no triple product-torus intersection, following its pair generators and transporting its domains, actual Spin-c labels and admissibility. Fix that representative. Compatible generic source-dependent perturbations, coherent over the required conformal faces and auxiliary parameter families, then make the disk and polygon spaces entering the hat differential, continuation, handleslide, stabilization and surgery operations regular with their actual expected dimensions. The common protected tensor and arbitrary constant product-angle end charts can be prescribed, and coherent perturbations can be arbitrarily small about a supplied compatible reference model. Auxiliary polygon and anchored-continuation parameter families here keep the autonomous end paths fixed and regular on the required energy budget; regular compatible parameter-boundary data may be retained. No slice-regularity assertion is made for arbitrary parameter-varying autonomous end paths. This does not assert regularity by almost-complex variations alone on an arbitrary fixed triple, or invariance under the preliminary curve choice.

Dimensions include every allowed conformal and auxiliary family parameter. Quotient only actual source automorphisms: longitudinal translation acts freely on autonomous nonconstant two-ended strips; an anchored source-dependent continuation strip and a three-marked triangle have no translation quotient. Every total zero-dimensional space used in a mod-two count is finite, across all its literal realized classes and with its specified labels. The one-dimensional spaces entering the chain-map, composition and homotopy identities compactify to actual compact one-manifolds. At fixed data their boundaries are precisely the matching rigid polygon–polygon conformal splittings and strip–polygon breakings. In an auxiliary family the broken configurations are the rigid joint fiber configurations at one common parameter, together with the prescribed parameter-boundary strata; they need not be products of individually rigid parameterized polygon spaces. Every such broken end has an exhaustive gluing collar. For the zero-basepoint operations no nonconstant sphere or one-torus boundary disk survives; thus the specified boundary-degeneration terms vanish, and there is no further escape or uncontrolled periodic-domain end. Boundary parity gives the differential square-zero identity and the polygon chain-map, composition and homotopy identities.

At symmetric rank zero retain the original empty systems and use the point target directly: the differential is zero, the matching constant triangle is counted once, higher rigid operations vanish, and the conformal and parameter boundary identities are the actual source-space identities. No triple-torus exclusion or free translation quotient is imposed on that point map.

This is the analytic count theorem. It does not construct a subordinate surgery diagram, prove that a named top generator is a cycle, identify the homology of a surgery total complex with a filling, or prove Heegaard-move invariance. Those remain duties of the respective operation constructions.

For a single diagram the full-module admissibility convention tests all intended Spin-c sectors, including empty sectors, and implies the required global weak domain condition.

In positive symmetric rank choose, among the auxiliary data, an arbitrarily small pointed Hamiltonian representative with no triple product-torus intersection, following its pair generators and transporting its domains, actual Spin-c labels and admissibility. Fix that representative. Compatible generic source-dependent perturbations, coherent over the required conformal faces and auxiliary parameter families, then make the disk and polygon spaces entering the hat differential, continuation, handleslide, stabilization and surgery operations regular with their actual expected dimensions. The common protected tensor and arbitrary constant product-angle end charts can be prescribed, and coherent perturbations can be arbitrarily small about a supplied compatible reference model. Auxiliary polygon and anchored-continuation parameter families here keep the autonomous end paths fixed and regular on the required energy budget; regular compatible parameter-boundary data may be retained. No slice-regularity assertion is made for arbitrary parameter-varying autonomous end paths. This does not assert regularity by almost-complex variations alone on an arbitrary fixed triple, or invariance under the preliminary curve choice.

Dimensions include every allowed conformal and auxiliary family parameter. Quotient only actual source automorphisms: longitudinal translation acts freely on autonomous nonconstant two-ended strips; an anchored source-dependent continuation strip and a three-marked triangle have no translation quotient. Every total zero-dimensional space used in a mod-two count is finite, across all its literal realized classes and with its specified labels. The one-dimensional spaces entering the chain-map, composition and homotopy identities compactify to actual compact one-manifolds. At fixed data their boundaries are precisely the matching rigid polygon–polygon conformal splittings and strip–polygon breakings. In an auxiliary family the broken configurations are the rigid joint fiber configurations at one common parameter, together with the prescribed parameter-boundary strata; they need not be products of individually rigid parameterized polygon spaces. Every such broken end has an exhaustive gluing collar. For the zero-basepoint operations no nonconstant sphere or one-torus boundary disk survives; thus the specified boundary-degeneration terms vanish, and there is no further escape or uncontrolled periodic-domain end. Boundary parity gives the differential square-zero identity and the polygon chain-map, composition and homotopy identities.

At symmetric rank zero retain the original empty systems and use the point target directly: the differential is zero, the matching constant triangle is counted once, higher rigid operations vanish, and the conformal and parameter boundary identities are the actual source-space identities. No triple-torus exclusion or free translation quotient is imposed on that point map.

This is the analytic count theorem. It does not construct a subordinate surgery diagram, prove that a named top generator is a cycle, identify the homology of a surgery total complex with a filling, or prove Heegaard-move invariance. Those remain duties of the respective operation constructions.

before.axiom_use: The diagram-reflection and conjugation arguments use the ACω analytic branch for Heegaard Floer disk counts. The full-AC plan edge remains separate.
before.statement: Let $K\subset S^3$ be a smooth oriented knot and let $C(K)=\mathrm{CFK}^{\infty}(K)$ be its normalized bifiltered complex over $\mathbb F_2[U,U^{-1}]$. The complex of the reverse mirror $-K$ is filtered-chain-homotopy equivalent to the dual complex $C(K)^*=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb F_2[U,U^{-1}]}(C(K),\mathbb F_2[U,U^{-1}])$, with dual differential $d\phi(x)=\phi(\partial x)$ and dual basis elements at negated bifiltration coordinates. These are distinct symmetries: duality negates both filtration coordinates, while conjugation exchanges them.

before.axiom_use: The analytic construction assumes AC_omega through the regularity and compactness supplier. Each map is indexed by one Spin-c structure; the composition law sums over extensions only when stated.
before.statement:
Let $(W,\Sigma,\mathcal A)$ be a decorated knot cobordism from $(Y_0,K_0)$ to $(Y_1,K_1)$, and fix $\mathfrak s\in\operatorname{Spin}^c(W)$. Choose a parametrized Kirby decomposition of $W$, together with finite balanced Heegaard data satisfying the strict strong-admissibility condition normalized at all $w$-marks for each specified Spin-c sector. For positive-rank triangle pieces choose the divisor-compatible nearly symmetric regular end paths and generic source-dependent almost-complex perturbations used for the full-marked triangle counts; at rank zero use the empty-product point model. Intermediate pieces may contain links with several components or more than one pair of basepoints. Use the colored multipointed modules with $g+n-1$ attaching curves in $\operatorname{Sym}^{g+n-1}(S)$, and specialize all $w$-colors to $U$ and all $z$-colors to $V$; the displayed doubly pointed formula is the $n=1$ case. For an elementary triangle piece with four-dimensional cobordism $W_r$ represented by a subordinate Heegaard triple $(S,\boldsymbol\alpha,\boldsymbol\beta,\boldsymbol\gamma,w,z)$, its triangle-count map has the form
$$
\mathbf x\longmapsto \sum_{\mathbf y}\ \sum_{\substack{\phi\in\pi_2(\mathbf x,\Theta^+_{\boldsymbol\beta\boldsymbol\gamma},\mathbf y)\\ \mu(\phi)=0,\ \mathfrak s(\phi)=\mathfrak s|_{W_r},\\ n_{w_i}(\phi),n_{z_i}(\phi)\ge0\ \text{for every marked point}}} \#_2\bigl(\mathcal M(\phi)\bigr)U^{\sum_i n_{w_i}(\phi)}V^{\sum_i n_{z_i}(\phi)}\mathbf y,
$$
where $\Theta^+_{\boldsymbol\beta\boldsymbol\gamma}$ denotes a chosen cycle representative of the distinguished top-degree homology class of the appropriate standard auxiliary Heegaard pair, $\mathfrak s(\phi)$ is the Spin-c structure determined by the triangle class on $W_r$, and all marked multiplicities in the sum are nonnegative. The restriction $\mathfrak s|_{W_r}$ is taken under the identification of this elementary cobordism with its Kirby piece. The other symbols and coefficient ring are as in the two-color target definition. For a chosen auxiliary cycle with finite support $\Theta=\sum_j p_j\theta_j$, with $p_j\in\mathbb F_2[U,V]$ and basis generators $\theta_j$, interpret the displayed formula by $\mathbb F_2[U,V]$-linearity as $\sum_j p_j F(\mathbf x,\theta_j)$ (or $\sum_j p_j F(\theta_j,\mathbf x)$ for the alpha-triple convention). The elementary 2-handle maps and band maps are triangle-count maps; the 0-, 1-, 3-, and 4-handle maps use the corresponding stabilization or destabilization maps; cylindrical changes of the dividing set use basepoint and quasi-stabilization maps. Compose the elementary maps in the chosen decomposition to obtain a representative
$$
\widetilde F_{W,\Sigma,\mathcal A,\mathfrak s,\mathcal K}: CFL^-_{UV}(Y_0,K_0,\mathfrak s|_{Y_0})\longrightarrow CFL^-_{UV}(Y_1,K_1,\mathfrak s|_{Y_1}).
$$
The subscript $\mathcal K$ records the chosen decomposition and auxiliary data. This is one map for one Spin-c structure; maps for different Spin-c structures are not summed unless a sum is explicitly specified. Independence from $\mathcal K$, regular data, and parametrization is a separate naturality assertion.

before.axiom_use: Assumes AC_omega for generic data and the countable family of admissible decompositions considered in the construction.
before.statement:
Let $(W,\Sigma,\mathcal A)$ be a decorated knot cobordism between doubly pointed knots in $S^3$, and let $\mathfrak s\in\operatorname{Spin}^c(W)$. The representative maps from any two parametrized Kirby decompositions and admissible regular Heegaard choices are filtered $\mathbb F_2[U,V]$-equivariantly chain homotopic. If the decorated cobordism is a composite of $(W_1,\Sigma_1,\mathcal A_1)$ followed by $(W_2,\Sigma_2,\mathcal A_2)$, then for fixed Spin-c structures $\mathfrak s_i$ on $W_i$,
$$
\widetilde F_{W_2,\Sigma_2,\mathcal A_2,\mathfrak s_2}\circ \widetilde F_{W_1,\Sigma_1,\mathcal A_1,\mathfrak s_1} \simeq \sum_{\substack{\mathfrak s\in\operatorname{Spin}^c(W)\\ \mathfrak s|_{W_i}=\mathfrak s_i,\ i=1,2}} \widetilde F_{W,\Sigma,\mathcal A,\mathfrak s}.
$$
The sum is over Spin-c structures on the glued cobordism restricting to the specified structures on the two pieces. For $W=S^3\times[0,1]$, $\operatorname{Spin}^c(W)$ has one element; the sum has one term if the specified structures on the pieces are its restrictions, and is empty otherwise. In the compatible case the composition law is ordinary composition up to filtered equivariant chain homotopy.

before.axiom_use: Assumes AC_omega through the link-level Khovanov homology groups and their diagram independence; the birth, death, and saddle maps use only the integral Frobenius algebra.
before.statement: Assume countable choice and fix a generic movie $M$ of a smooth oriented surface cobordism $\Sigma$ from an oriented link $L_0$ to an oriented link $L_1$. For each regular frame $D$, let $Kh(D)$ be the normalized integral Khovanov homology group. The empty frame has the one-term complex $\mathbb Z$ in both gradings zero, using the empty resolution and the zero-fold tensor product. Associate to a birth the unit map $\eta:\mathbb Z\to\mathcal A$, $\eta(1)=1$; associate to a death the counit $\epsilon:\mathcal A\to\mathbb Z$, $\epsilon(1)=0,\epsilon(X)=1$; and associate to a saddle the multiplication $m:\mathcal A\otimes\mathcal A\to\mathcal A$ when two resolution circles merge, or the comultiplication $\Delta:\mathcal A\to\mathcal A\otimes\mathcal A$ when one splits. Each local map is tensored with the identity on unaffected circles. Associate to planar isotopy the induced identification of the cube complexes. For Reidemeister moves, use the following fixed Bar-Natan constructions: the kink retractions $F_+=v-\Delta$, $G_+=e$, $F_-=u$, $G_-=w-m$; the two inverse-crossing strong retractions with degree-zero inclusion $(1,ut)^T$ and projection $(1,-se)$, with their specified reverse-order cube signs; and the third-move equivalences obtained by the explicit source- or target-cone retractions onto the common six-point residual complex. Here $u,e$ are circle birth/death, $v,w$ are punctured-torus birth/death, and the saddle letters denote the actual local bands in these constructions. Use their specified inverses for the reversed moves. Insert these formal surface matrices into the fixed planar outside of the diagram, then apply the integral Frobenius cobordism functor. Normalize a state $v$ to cochain degree $|v|-n_-$ and quantum shift $|v|+n_+-2n_-$. Fix the local coordinate identifications and orientation cases once, with the Koszul crossing-order correction $(-1)^{v(a)v(b)}$ when crossings $a,b$ are interchanged. These local maps are chosen once; composing them with an arbitrary automorphism of a complex is not an allowed change of representative. Compose the induced maps on homology in movie order and denote the result by $Kh(M):Kh(L_0)\to Kh(L_1)$, considered modulo multiplication by $-1$. This definition fixes a movie; independence from changing the movie is not included in the definition.

before.axiom_use: Assumes AC_omega through link-level Khovanov homology and the oriented link invariance theorem; no full Axiom of Choice is used.
before.statement:
Assume countable choice. Let $\Sigma\subset S^3\times[0,1]$ be a compact smooth oriented cobordism from an oriented knot $K_0$ to an oriented knot $K_1$, with fixed product collars and fixed endpoint diagrams. Every generic movie $M$ of $\Sigma$ defines a map of bidegree $(0,\chi(\Sigma))$,
$$
Kh(M):Kh^{i,j}(K_0)\longrightarrow Kh^{i,j+\chi(\Sigma)}(K_1),
$$
where $\chi(\Sigma)$ is the Euler characteristic of the surface and the integral even Khovanov groups use the normalized crossing shifts. If two such movies represent cobordisms related by an ambient isotopy fixed on the boundary collars, their maps differ by multiplication by a single overall sign, independent of the input class. The resulting assignment is a functor after each morphism set is quotiented by the action $f\mapsto -f$; before that quotient the sign is not canonical.

before.axiom_use: The integral Khovanov branch assumes AC_omega through link invariance. The two-color knot Floer branch is over F2[U,V] and is indexed by Spin-c structures, with the composition sum over extensions.
before.statement: Assume countable choice. For a smooth oriented knot cobordism in $S^3\times[0,1]$, the ordinary even integral Khovanov assignment has source and target the bigraded groups $Kh^{i,j}$ and is defined up to an overall sign; after quotienting each Khovanov hom-set by the action $f\mapsto -f$, it is invariant under ambient isotopy fixed on the boundary and respects composition. If the surface is equipped with a dividing set and one $w$- and one $z$-basepoint on each boundary knot, the decorated knot Floer assignment has source and target the filtered complexes $CFL^-_{UV}(S^3,K)$ over $\mathbb F_2[U,V]$, and is invariant up to filtered equivariant chain homotopy. For a general gluing of decorated four-dimensional cobordisms, the link Floer composition law sums over Spin-c structures on the composite that restrict to the chosen structures on the pieces; for the product $S^3\times[0,1]$, this sum has one term if the chosen piece structures are restrictions of the unique product structure, and is empty otherwise. In the compatible case the law is ordinary composition. The two assignments therefore have separately specified targets, coefficient rings, decorations, and equivalence relations.

before.statement:
Let $\mathcal A=\mathbb Z[X]/(X^2)$ with unit $\eta(1)=1$ and counit $\epsilon(1)=0,\epsilon(X)=1$. On a movie with one unaffected circle, birth a disjoint circle and then cap that same circle by a death. The composite operator is
$$
\mathcal A\xrightarrow{\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal A}\otimes\eta} \mathcal A\otimes\mathcal A\xrightarrow{\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal A}\otimes\epsilon} \mathcal A,
$$
which is zero and therefore is not the identity, even after allowing multiplication by an overall sign.

```tikz
\begin{tikzcd}
\mathcal A
\arrow[r, "{\operatorname{id}\otimes\eta}"]
& \mathcal A\otimes\mathcal A
\arrow[r, "{\operatorname{id}\otimes\epsilon}"]
& \mathcal A
\end{tikzcd}
```

The movie is a cylinder on the original circle disjoint union a born-and-capped sphere; the diagram specifies the local birth and death sequence and is not used as a proof.

before.statement:
Let $K\subset S^3$ be a smooth oriented knot smoothly concordant to the unknot. Then there are finite-rank free $\mathbb F_2[U,U^{-1}]$ bifiltered chain complexes $A$ and $B$, each having zero total homology, such that
$$ \mathrm{CFK}^{\infty}(K)\oplus A\simeq \Lambda\oplus B, $$
where $\Lambda=\mathbb F_2[U,U^{-1}]$ is the normalized unknot complex with zero differential and generator in Maslov grading and both filtration coordinates zero, and $\simeq$ is a Maslov-graded filtered chain homotopy equivalence whose maps and homotopies do not increase either filtration. The acyclic summands are acyclic only after the filtrations are forgotten; no acyclicity of their associated-graded complexes is asserted.

before.axiom_use: The finite filtered threshold argument and the least-integer definition use no choice. The planned analytic cobordism branch uses ACω as declared by its suppliers; full AC is not inferred or used.
before.statement:
Let $K\subset S^3$ be a smooth oriented knot and let $C(K)=\mathrm{CFK}^{\infty}(K)$ have a finite homogeneous basis $x_1,\ldots,x_m$ with Maslov grading $M(x_r)$ and Alexander filtration $A(x_r)$. Let $C^-(K)$ be the subcomplex spanned over $\mathbb F_2[U]$ by $U^n x_r$ for $n\ge0$, with $M(U^n x_r)=M(x_r)-2n$ and $A(U^n x_r)=A(x_r)-n$, and assume $H_*(C^-(K))\cong\mathbb F_2[U]$ with generator in Maslov degree zero. For each integer $s$, let $\mathcal A(K,s)$ be the subcomplex spanned over $\mathbb F_2$ by those terms $U^n x_r$ with $n\ge0$ and $A(x_r)-n\le s$. For any Maslov-graded $\mathbb F_2[U]$ complex $D$, let $\delta(D)$ be the maximal Maslov grading of a homogeneous non-torsion class in $H_*(D)$, with $\delta(D)=-\infty$ if no such class exists. Define $\nu^-(K)$ to be the least integer $s$ for which $\delta(\mathcal A(K,s))=0$. Then
$$ 0\le \nu^-(K)\le g_4^{\mathrm{sm}}(K), $$
where $g_4^{\mathrm{sm}}(K)$ is the minimum genus of a smooth compact connected oriented properly embedded surface in the four-ball bounded by $K$.

before.axiom_use: The finite hook, tensor, grid-rank and staircase arguments are choice-free. Actual normalized knot models and geometric comparisons reuse the supplied countable-choice interfaces; the approved separate full-AC dependency is retained.
before.statement:
Let $K$ and $J$ be smooth oriented knots, and use the epsilon sign convention from the preceding definition. If their knot Floer complexes are stably filtered equivalent, meaning that there are totally acyclic bifiltered complexes $A$ and $B$ with $\mathrm{CFK}^{\infty}(K)\oplus A$ filtered-chain-homotopy equivalent to $\mathrm{CFK}^{\infty}(J)\oplus B$, then $\epsilon(K)=\epsilon(J)$. The acyclic summands here need not be acyclic after taking either associated-graded filtration.

The invariant satisfies $\epsilon(-K)=-\epsilon(K)$, $\epsilon(K)=0\Rightarrow\tau(K)=0$, and the tensor rules
$$ \epsilon(K)=\epsilon(J)\Rightarrow\epsilon(K\#J)=\epsilon(K),\qquad \epsilon(K)=0\Rightarrow\epsilon(K\#J)=\epsilon(J). $$
The converse of $\epsilon(K)=0\Rightarrow\tau(K)=0$ fails: the knot $T_{2,5}\#-T_{4,5}\#T_{2,3;2,5}$ has $\tau=0$ and $\epsilon=1$, where $T_{p,q}$ is the positive $(p,q)$ torus knot and $T_{2,3;2,5}$ is the $(2,5)$ cable of the right-handed trefoil with longitudinal winding two. Epsilon is not an integer-valued homomorphism on the smooth concordance group: the right-handed trefoil has $\epsilon=1$ and its connected sum with itself also has $\epsilon=1$, not $2$.

before.statement:
Let $G$ be any $n\times n$ grid diagram representing a smooth oriented knot $K\subset S^3$. Form the diagonal grid complex by setting every marking variable $U_i$ equal to a single variable $U$, and define $\Upsilon_G(t)$ by the t-modified non-torsion grading on that complex for $0\le t\le1$, extended by $\Upsilon_G(t)=\Upsilon_G(2-t)$ for $1<t\le2$. Then for every $t\in[0,2]$,
$$ \Upsilon_G(t)=\Upsilon_K(t), $$
where $\Upsilon_K$ is the finite cycle-minimax invariant defined from $\mathrm{CFK}^{\infty}(K)$. In this statement the quotient with all $U_i$ identified carries the factor $W^{\otimes(n-1)}$, where $W$ has generators in Maslov/Alexander bidegrees $(0,0)$ and $(-1,-1)$; this factor is retained in the proof and is not counted as an improvement to the grid-state complexity bound.
