before.statement:
For every smooth oriented knot $K\subset S^3$, the function $\Upsilon_K:[0,2]\to\mathbb R$ defined by the finite cycle minimax is continuous and piecewise linear with finitely many breakpoints, satisfies $\Upsilon_K(0)=0$ and $\Upsilon_K(t)=\Upsilon_K(2-t)$, and has right derivative $\Upsilon'_K(0+)=-\tau(K)$. For smooth oriented knots $K,J$ and $t\in[0,2]$,
$$ \Upsilon_{K\#J}(t)=\Upsilon_K(t)+\Upsilon_J(t),\qquad \Upsilon_{-K}(t)=-\Upsilon_K(t), $$
where $-K$ is the reverse mirror, the inverse under connected sum in the smooth concordance group. If $g_4^{\mathrm{sm}}(K)$ is the minimum genus of a smooth properly embedded compact connected oriented surface in the four-ball with boundary $K$, then
$$ |\Upsilon_K(t)|\le t\,g_4^{\mathrm{sm}}(K)\qquad(0\le t\le1). $$

after.statement:
For the knot-level assertions, assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. For every smooth oriented knot $K\subset S^3$, the function $\Upsilon_K:[0,2]\to\mathbb R$ defined by the finite cycle minimax is continuous and piecewise linear with finitely many breakpoints, satisfies $\Upsilon_K(0)=0$ and $\Upsilon_K(t)=\Upsilon_K(2-t)$, and has right derivative $\Upsilon'_K(0+)=-\tau(K)$. For smooth oriented knots $K,J$ and $t\in[0,2]$,
$$ \Upsilon_{K\#J}(t)=\Upsilon_K(t)+\Upsilon_J(t),\qquad \Upsilon_{-K}(t)=-\Upsilon_K(t), $$
where $-K$ is the reverse mirror, the inverse under connected sum in the smooth concordance group. If $g_4^{\mathrm{sm}}(K)$ is the minimum genus of a smooth properly embedded compact connected oriented surface in the four-ball with boundary $K$, then
$$ |\Upsilon_K(t)|\le t\,g_4^{\mathrm{sm}}(K)\qquad(0\le t\le1). $$

before.statement:
Let $\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sm}}$ be the smooth knot concordance group, with addition induced by oriented connected sum and inverse represented by reverse mirror. The function $\epsilon: \mathcal C_{\mathrm{sm}}\to\{-1,0,1\}$ is well-defined and concordance-invariant, but it is not a homomorphism to $\mathbb Z$. The map
$$ \Upsilon:\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sm}}\longrightarrow \mathrm{PL}([0,2],\mathbb R),\qquad [K]\longmapsto\Upsilon_K, $$
is a group homomorphism, where $\mathrm{PL}([0,2],\mathbb R)$ is the abelian group of continuous piecewise-linear real-valued functions under pointwise addition. For every representative $K$ and $0\le t\le1$, its value satisfies $|\Upsilon_K(t)|\le t\,g_4^{\mathrm{sm}}(K)$.

before.statement:
Let $T_{2,3}$ be the right-handed trefoil and $-T_{2,3}$ its reverse mirror. A filtered basis for $\mathrm{CFK}^{\infty}(T_{2,3})$ is $x_0,x_1,x_2$ with $(M,A)(x_0)=(0,1)$, $(M,A)(x_1)=(-1,0)$, $(M,A)(x_2)=(-2,-1)$ and differential $\partial x_1=Ux_0+x_2$, $\partial x_0=\partial x_2=0$. Under the conventions of this page,
$$ \epsilon(T_{2,3})=1,\qquad \Upsilon_{T_{2,3}}(t)=\begin{cases}-t,&0\le t\le1,\\ t-2,&1\le t\le2.\end{cases} $$
The graph has its unique interior breakpoint at $t=1$. For the reverse mirror, $\epsilon(-T_{2,3})=-1$ and $\Upsilon_{-T_{2,3}}(t)=-\Upsilon_{T_{2,3}}(t)$.

references.title: Andras Juhasz, Floer homology and surface decompositions, arXiv:math/0609779v3, §§2 and 9
references.locator: Printed pp.3–5 and 31–38; balanced and taut sutured manifolds, horizontal decompositions, and the rank-one/product criterion

before.statement:
A **sutured manifold** $(M,\gamma)$ consists of a compact oriented $3$-manifold $M$ with boundary and a union $\gamma$ of pairwise disjoint annuli and tori in $\partial M$. Each annulus contains a suture, its oriented core circle; write $A(\gamma)$ for the annuli and $s(\gamma)$ for the union of their cores. Orient each component of $R(\gamma)=\partial M\setminus\operatorname{int}(\gamma)$ so that its boundary orientation agrees in the annulus with the homology class of the suture. The regions whose normal points out of $M$ form $R_+(\gamma)$ and those whose normal points into $M$ form $R_-(\gamma)$. The sutured manifold is **balanced** when $M$ has no closed component, $\chi(R_+)=\chi(R_-)$, and every component of $\partial M$ meets an annular component of $\gamma$. It is **irreducible** when every embedded $2$-sphere in $M$ bounds a $3$-ball in $M$. A properly embedded surface $S$ is **incompressible** when it has no compressing disk. A compressing disk is an embedded disk $D\subset M$ with $\partial D\subset S$, $D\cap S=\partial D$, and $\partial D$ an essential simple closed curve in $S$ (that is, it does not bound a disk in $S$). For a compact surface $S$ put $x(S)=\sum_{S_j}\max(0,-\chi(S_j))$, where the sum is over its connected components. The Thurston norm $x(\alpha)$ of a relative homology class $\alpha\in H_2(M,\gamma;\mathbb Z)$ is the minimum of $x(S)$ over properly embedded oriented representatives $S$ with $\partial S\subset\gamma$ and $[S]=\alpha$. Such a representative is **norm-minimizing** when it is incompressible and $x(S)=x(\alpha)$. A balanced sutured manifold is **taut** when it is irreducible and $R(\gamma)$ is norm-minimizing in $H_2(M,\gamma;\mathbb Z)$.

A **product sutured manifold** is $(R\times[0,1],\partial R\times[0,1])$ for a compact oriented surface $R$, with positive and negative regions $R\times\{1\}$ and $R\times\{0\}$. A properly embedded oriented surface $S\subset M$ is a **decomposing surface** when every component $\lambda$ of $S\cap\gamma$ is either a properly embedded nonseparating arc in an annular component meeting its suture once, a simple closed curve in an annular component homologous to that suture, or a homotopically nontrivial curve in a toroidal component, with all such curves in one torus component representing the same homology class. A **product disk** is a decomposing surface that is a disk and meets the sutures in exactly two points. A **product annulus** is a decomposing annulus with one boundary circle in $R_+$ and one in $R_-$. A **horizontal surface** $S$ in a balanced sutured manifold has no closed component, $|\partial S|=|s(\gamma)|$, $[S]=[R_+]$ in $H_2(M,\gamma;\mathbb Z)$, and $\chi(S)=\chi(R_+)$. The sutured manifold is **vertically prime** when every horizontal surface is parallel to $R_+$ or $R_-$, where parallel means that the surfaces cobound an embedded product between them.

When $(M,\gamma)$ is irreducible, $\gamma$ has no torus component, and $R_+$ and $R_-$ are incompressible and diffeomorphic, a **product region** is a submanifold $\Phi\times[0,1]\subset M$ for a compact possibly disconnected surface $\Phi$ such that $\Phi\times\{0\}$ and $\Phi\times\{1\}$ are incompressible subsurfaces of $R_-$ and $R_+$, respectively. A **characteristic product region** is a product region $E\times[0,1]$ such that every product region $\Phi\times[0,1]$ can be carried into it by an ambient isotopy of $M$.

before.statement:
For a balanced sutured manifold $(M,\gamma)$, a **balanced sutured Heegaard diagram** is a tuple $\mathcal H=(\Sigma,\boldsymbol\alpha,\boldsymbol\beta)$ where $\Sigma$ is a compact oriented surface with boundary and each of $\boldsymbol\alpha,\boldsymbol\beta$ is a finite family of pairwise disjoint simple closed curves in $\operatorname{int}\Sigma$. It defines $M$ by attaching $3$-dimensional $2$-handles to $\Sigma\times[0,1]$ along $\boldsymbol\alpha\times\{0\}$ and $\boldsymbol\beta\times\{1\}$, with sutures $\partial\Sigma\times\{1/2\}$ on $\gamma=\partial\Sigma\times[0,1]$. The diagram is balanced when the two families have equal cardinality $d$ and the natural maps from components of $\partial\Sigma$ to components of $\Sigma\setminus\bigcup\boldsymbol\alpha$ and $\Sigma\setminus\bigcup\boldsymbol\beta$ are both surjective. A **domain** is an integral two-chain generated by the closures of regions of $\Sigma\setminus(\bigcup\boldsymbol\alpha\cup\bigcup\boldsymbol\beta)$ disjoint from $\partial\Sigma$. A **periodic domain** is a domain whose boundary is an integral sum of full $\alpha$- and $\beta$-curves. The diagram is **admissible** when each nonzero periodic domain has at least one positive and one negative region coefficient.

The symmetric product $\operatorname{Sym}^d(\Sigma)=\Sigma^d/S_d$ is the space of unordered $d$-tuples of points. The product tori $\mathbb T_\alpha,\mathbb T_\beta$ are the images of the products of the $d$ attaching curves in this symmetric product. A **generator** is a point of $\mathbb T_\alpha\cap\mathbb T_\beta$, equivalently a collection of $d$ transverse intersection points, one on each attaching curve in each family. A **Whitney disk class** from generator $\mathbf{x}$ to generator $\mathbf{y}$ is a relative homotopy class of maps of a disk into $\operatorname{Sym}^d(\Sigma)$ whose two boundary arcs lie on the product tori and whose endpoints are $\mathbf{x},\mathbf{y}$; $\pi_2(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{y})$ denotes the set of these classes. Fix a smooth path $J_t$ of almost complex structures on $\operatorname{Sym}^d(\Sigma)$, where an almost complex structure is a smooth bundle endomorphism $J$ with $J^2=-\operatorname{id}$. A representative of a Whitney disk class is a smooth strip $u:\mathbb R\times[0,1]\to\operatorname{Sym}^d(\Sigma)$ satisfying $\partial_su+J_t(u)\partial_tu=0$, with $u(s,0)\in\mathbb T_\alpha$, $u(s,1)\in\mathbb T_\beta$, and limits $\mathbf{x},\mathbf{y}$ as $s\to-\infty,+\infty$. Its Maslov index is the Fredholm index of the linearized Cauchy--Riemann operator at a representative, and $\mathcal M_J(\phi)$ denotes the space of representatives of class $\phi$. Translation of the real coordinate gives the $\mathbb R$ action on this moduli space.

When $d=0$, $\operatorname{Sym}^0(\Sigma)$ is a point, both product tori are that point, and the unique generator is the empty collection.

A **periodic domain** is an integral two-chain of regions of $\Sigma$ whose boundary is an integral sum of attaching curves and whose boundary coefficient on $\partial\Sigma$ is zero. Its coefficients are its multiplicities on the regions. The diagram is **admissible** when every nonzero periodic domain has at least one positive and one negative region coefficient. A Whitney disk from generator $\mathbf x$ to generator $\mathbf y$ is a relative homotopy class of maps of a disk into $\operatorname{Sym}^d(\Sigma)$ whose two boundary arcs lie on the product tori and whose endpoints are $\mathbf x$ and $\mathbf y$. Its Maslov index is the Fredholm index of the linearized Cauchy--Riemann operator at a representative. A coherent orientation system assigns orientations to these operators' determinant lines compatibly with gluing.

For a fixed admissible diagram, the **sutured Floer disk-count module** $SFC(\mathcal H;R)$ is the free $R$-module on its generators, where $R=\mathbb F_2$ or $\mathbb Z$. For $R=\mathbb F_2$, its formal differential counts translation classes modulo two:
$$\partial\mathbf{x}=\sum_{\mathbf{y}}\sum_{\substack{\phi\in\pi_2(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{y})\\\mu(\phi)=1}}\#_2\bigl(\mathcal M_J(\phi)/\mathbb R\bigr)\,\mathbf{y}.$$
For $R=\mathbb Z$, use a coherent orientation system, which assigns orientations to determinant lines of the linearized disk operators compatibly with gluing, and replace $\#_2$ by the signed count $\#_{\mathfrak o}$. The homology of this diagram-level differential is denoted $H_*(SFC(\mathcal H;R))$ once the moduli counts are finite and the differential squares to zero. When $d=0$ the unique empty generator has zero differential. Once admissible diagram-change maps are proved to be chain homotopy equivalences, their common homology is denoted $SFH(M,\gamma;R)$. This definition fixes the chain-level and coefficient conventions; it does not assert analytic compactness, gluing, invariance, or surface-decomposition results.

before.statement:
Let $(M,\gamma)$ be a balanced sutured manifold. Fix a nowhere-zero vector field $v_0$ along $\partial M$ that points into $M$ on $R_-(\gamma)$, points out of $M$ on $R_+(\gamma)$, and on each annular suture region follows the gradient of a height coordinate whose level circles are the sutures. A **sutured Spin-c structure** is a homology class of nowhere-zero vector fields $v$ on $M$ whose boundary restriction is $v_0$. Two such fields are homologous when, outside some open ball in $\operatorname{int}M$, they are homotopic through nowhere-zero fields fixed on $\partial M$. The set of these classes is denoted $\operatorname{Spin}^c(M,\gamma)$.

For a balanced Heegaard diagram of $(M,\gamma)$ and a generator $\mathbf{x}$, choose a Morse function compatible with the diagram. The generator specifies the multi-trajectory joining its paired index-one and index-two critical points. Modify the gradient in a regular neighborhood of that trajectory to obtain a nowhere-zero vector field agreeing with $v_0$ on $\partial M$; for this chosen Morse data its homology class is denoted $\mathfrak{s}(\mathbf{x})$. The theorem that the assignment is independent of auxiliary Morse and gradient choices is part of diagram invariance, not asserted by this definition. The chain subcomplex generated by generators assigned to a fixed class $\mathfrak{s}$ has homology denoted $SFH(M,\gamma,\mathfrak{s};R)$ for coefficients $R$ whenever the diagram-level differential is defined. For a chosen trivialization $t$ of the oriented plane field $v_0^\perp$ along $\partial M$, the relative Chern class $c_1(\mathfrak{s},t)\in H^2(M,\partial M;\mathbb Z)$ is the relative Euler obstruction to extending $t$ over $v^\perp$, where $v$ represents $\mathfrak{s}$ and the plane orientation is determined by the orientation of $M$ and the direction of $v$.

For an oriented null-homologous knot $K$ in a closed connected oriented $3$-manifold $Y$, let $M=Y\setminus\operatorname{int}N(K)$ and let $\gamma_\mu$ be the union of two disjoint annuli on $\partial M$ whose core sutures are parallel meridians of $K$ with opposite orientations. A Seifert surface is regarded in $M$ after deleting a collar of its boundary, so it determines a relative class on the sutured knot exterior. The meridional direction supplies the boundary trivialization of $v_0^\perp$ used to normalize the relative Chern-class pairing.

before.title: Admissible instanton surgery-triangle data

references.title: P. B. Kronheimer and T. S. Mrowka, Dehn surgery, the fundamental group and SU(2), §§2–4

before.axiom_use: The full Axiom of Choice is retained for the generic perturbation, regularity, and compactness constructions required by later theorems; no such existence or regularity conclusion is asserted by this definition.
before.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $K\subset S^3$ be a smooth knot with chosen exterior $E_K$ and ordered meridian-longitude basis $(\mu,\lambda)$. A **surgery triad** is a cyclically ordered triple of primitive unoriented slopes $s_0,s_1,s_\infty$ on $\partial E_K$ whose pairwise geometric intersection numbers are one, together with the oriented fillings $Y_j=E_K(s_j)$ and the three 2-handle surgery cobordisms in the cyclic order $Y_0\to Y_1\to Y_\infty\to Y_0$. Choose primitive representatives $v_j=(p_j,q_j)$ in the ordered basis $(\mu,\lambda)$ so that $\det(v_0,v_1)=\det(v_1,v_\infty)=\det(v_\infty,v_0)=1$; the cyclic order is the one for which this orientation convention holds. The geometric intersection number of $s_j$ and $s_k$ is $|p_jq_k-p_kq_j|$.

For a closed oriented Riemannian 3-manifold $Y$, a principal $SO(3)$-bundle $P\to Y$ is a locally trivial bundle with fiber $SO(3)$ and right structure-group action. A connection $A$ is a smooth right-$SO(3)$-invariant horizontal distribution on $P$ complementary to its vertical tangent spaces. In a local trivialization its curvature is $F_A=dA+\tfrac12[A\wedge A]$; it is **flat** when $F_A=0$. Let $\mathcal A(P)$ be the space of smooth connections and let $\mathcal G(P)$ be the group of bundle automorphisms covering the identity of $Y$. The configuration space is the quotient $\mathcal B(P)=\mathcal A(P)/\mathcal G(P)$. The associated oriented rank-three real vector bundle has second Stiefel–Whitney class $w_2(P)\in H^2(Y;\mathbb Z/2)$.

Fix an $SO(3)$-invariant inner product on $\mathfrak{so}(3)$ and normalize the Chern–Simons functional on its covering of $\mathcal B(P)$ so that its differential at $A$ in a connection variation $a$ is $d\mathrm{CS}_A(a)=\int_Y\langle a\wedge F_A\rangle$. A **holonomy perturbation** is a finite sum of gauge-invariant terms formed by integrating smooth class functions of holonomy around a finite family of embedded loops against compactly supported smooth weights. A critical point of a perturbed Chern–Simons functional is called a perturbed flat connection. At a nondegenerate critical point, the gauge-fixed Hessian is self-adjoint; the **spectral flow** along a path of such Hessians is the signed count of eigenvalues crossing zero and supplies the relative grading convention. Give $\mathbb R\times Y$ the product metric and orientation $dt\wedge\mathrm{or}(Y)$. Fix a holonomy perturbation $f_\pi$ and write $V_\pi(B)=\nabla_{L^2}f_\pi(B)$ for its gradient. A **finite-energy perturbed anti-self-dual trajectory** is a gauge-equivalence class with a temporal-gauge representative $A=B(t)$ on the pullback bundle satisfying
$$\frac{dB}{dt}=-\bigl(*_YF_B+V_\pi(B)\bigr)=-\nabla_{L^2}(\mathrm{CS}+f_\pi)(B),$$
with specified limiting critical points $\beta_-,\beta_+$ of that same perturbed functional at the two ends, and with finite flow energy
$$E_\pi(B):=\int_{\mathbb R}\left\|\frac{dB}{dt}\right\|_{L^2(Y)}^2\,dt=\int_{\mathbb R}\|*_YF_B+V_\pi(B)\|_{L^2(Y)}^2\,dt<\infty.$$
Equivalently, in this gauge its four-dimensional equation is $F_A^++\widehat V_\pi(A)=0$, where $\widehat V_\pi(A)=\tfrac12(dt\wedge V_\pi(B)+*_YV_\pi(B))$. When $\pi=0$ this reduces to the ordinary anti-self-duality equation. On a chosen real lift of the Chern–Simons functional along the trajectory, the chain rule gives $d(\mathrm{CS}+f_\pi)(B(t))/dt=-\|dB/dt\|_{L^2}^2$; whenever the functional has the specified endpoint limits, the energy is their difference. For nonzero perturbations those endpoints need not be flat, so no finiteness of the unperturbed curvature integral $\int_{\mathbb R\times Y}|F_A|^2$ is imposed. If the analytic Fredholm construction is established, the expected dimension is the index of the gauge-fixed linearization of the perturbed equation with the stated asymptotic conditions; translation decreases dimension by one for a nonconstant trajectory.

The **candidate instanton surgery-triangle input data** consist of a principal $SO(3)$-bundle on each $Y_j$, compatible bundle identifications on the three cobordisms, the invariant inner product and Chern–Simons normalization, the allowed perturbation class, and the grading convention. After separate proofs of analytic existence, regularity, compactness and gluing, these data may be used to define critical-point complexes and cobordism maps. Chain complexes, exactness of the three-term Floer sequence, and independence of the choices are separate theorem obligations. This definition asserts none of those analytic or Floer-theoretic conclusions.

before.title: Boundary slope of an incompressible surface in a knot exterior
before.statement: Assume full AC. Let $K\subset S^3$ be a smooth oriented knot with chosen compact exterior $E_K$ and boundary torus $T_K=\partial E_K$. A simple closed curve on a surface is **essential** if it is not null-homotopic there. A surface $S\subset E_K$ is properly embedded if $S\cap\partial E_K=\partial S$ and its interior lies in the interior of $E_K$. It is **incompressible** if it has no embedded disk with interior disjoint from $S$ and essential boundary in $S$; it is **boundary-incompressible** if it has no embedded disk whose boundary is the union of an arc in $S$ that does not cut off a disk and an arc in $\partial E_K$. A **boundary slope** of $K$ is the unoriented isotopy class of an essential simple closed curve on $T_K$ that occurs as the boundary of a properly embedded, orientable, incompressible, boundary-incompressible surface. Using the positive meridian $\mu$ and preferred longitude $\lambda$ as a homology basis, a primitive class $a[\lambda]+b[\mu]$ has slope $b/a\in\mathbb Q\cup\{\infty\}$, with $a=0$ interpreted as $\infty$. A boundary slope is **strict** if it has a realizing orientable, incompressible, boundary-incompressible surface which is not a fiber of any locally trivial fibration $E_K\to S^1$; a fiber is the inverse image of a point under that bundle projection.

references.title: Allen Hatcher, Boundary Slopes of Incompressible Surfaces
John A. Baldwin and Steven Sivek, Torus knots, the A-polynomial, and SL(2,C), §4.1

after.title: Boundary slope of an incompressible surface in a knot exterior
after.statement: Assume full AC. Let $K\subset S^3$ be a smooth oriented knot with chosen compact exterior $E_K$ and boundary torus $T_K=\partial E_K$. A **boundary slope** of $K$ is the unoriented isotopy class of an essential simple closed curve on $T_K$ that occurs as a boundary component of a connected, properly embedded, orientable, incompressible, boundary-incompressible surface. Using the positive meridian $\mu$ and preferred longitude $\lambda$ as a homology basis, a primitive class $a[\lambda]+b[\mu]$ has slope $b/a\in\mathbb Q\cup\{\infty\}$, with $a=0$ interpreted as $\infty$. A boundary slope is **strict** if it has a connected realizing orientable, incompressible, boundary-incompressible surface which is not a fiber of any locally trivial fibration $E_K\to S^1$; a fiber is the inverse image of a point under that bundle projection.

before.title: SL2(C)-abelian surgery
before.statement: Assume full AC. Let $K\subset S^3$ be a smooth oriented knot, let $p,q\in\mathbb Z$ be coprime and not both zero, and let $E_K(p/q)$ be the Dehn filling whose attached solid-torus meridian is identified with $p[\mu]+q[\lambda]$. A closed 3-manifold $Y$ is **$SL_2(\mathbb C)$-abelian** if every homomorphism $\pi_1(Y)\to SL_2(\mathbb C)$ has abelian image. The slope $p/q$ is an **$SL_2(\mathbb C)$-abelian surgery slope** for $K$ if $E_K(p/q)$ is $SL_2(\mathbb C)$-abelian. The knot admits infinitely many such surgeries if infinitely many distinct rational slopes have this property.

before.title: A nonseparating longitudinal surface in a fibered exterior is a fiber
before.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $K\subset S^3$ be a fibered knot with exterior $E_K$ and fiber surface $F$. If $S\subset E_K$ is a connected, orientable, nonseparating, incompressible properly embedded surface whose boundary is a nonempty union of longitudes, then $S$ is isotopic to $F$. After their boundary curves are identified by an isotopy in the boundary torus and this alignment is extended across a collar, the concluding isotopy may be taken relative to the aligned boundary.

references.title: Ozsváth and Szabó, On the Heegaard Floer homology of branched double-covers, Propositions 6.1 and 6.2

before.axiom_use: Uses the ACω analytic branch of Heegaard Floer theory; the unlink topology computation itself is choice-free.
before.statement: For every integer $k\ge1$, let $U_k\subset S^3$ be a $k$-component planar unlink with an arbitrary orientation on each component, and choose a basepoint $p$ on any one component. Its double branched cover is $\#^{\,k-1}(S^2\times S^1)$, with $\Sigma(U_1)=S^3$. Over $\mathbb F_2$, the hat Floer group of this cover is identified with the exterior algebra on a $(k-1)$-dimensional vector space, hence has rank $2^{k-1}$. Under these identifications, the cobordism maps for saddle cobordisms between neighboring unlink resolutions, with $p$ carried outside the saddle disk, are the multiplication and comultiplication maps of the two-dimensional Frobenius algebra $\mathbb F_2[X]/(X^2)$ after reduction at the marked component. The identification includes the marked-circle cases and fixes the basis conventions needed to compare the first surgery differential with the reduced Khovanov cube.

before.title: Encoded diagram size and exact output
before.statement:
Let $D$ be a nonempty finite regular oriented link diagram: a projection of a finite union of oriented circles with finitely many transverse double points, no triple points, and one overpassing branch specified at each double point. Let $c(D)$ be its number of crossings and $m(D)$ its number of components. An arc is a connected strand segment cut at each undercrossing; each component with no undercrossings contributes one closed arc. Write $a(D)$ for the number of arcs. If $q(D)$ components have no undercrossings, then $a(D)=c(D)+q(D)$ and $0\le q(D)\le m(D)$.

A supplied finite code for $D$ has code length $L$, the total number of bits in that literal code, including its tags, signs, labels, and separators. The length depends on the chosen encoding. In particular, for one of the tagged Gauss, signed Dowker–Thistlethwaite, or oriented planar-diagram formats, $L$ is the bit length of the supplied valid code in that format. The procedures in this page take typed mathematical diagrams or valid codes as stated; no string parser or malformed-code behavior is included in any operation count.

For an integer $z$, define its signed-magnitude bit length by $\ell_{\mathbb Z}(0)=1$ and $\ell_{\mathbb Z}(z)=1+\lceil\log_2(|z|+1)\rceil$ for $z\ne0$. For a Laurent polynomial $P(A)=\sum_{j\in\mathbb Z}z_jA^j$ with finite support, define its coefficient-bit size as $0$ if $P=0$, and otherwise as $\max_{j:z_j\ne0}\ell_{\mathbb Z}(z_j)$. Its absolute Laurent degree is $\max_{j:z_j\ne0}|j|$, with value $0$ for $P=0$. For a prime $p$, elements of $\mathbb F_p$ are represented exactly by residues $0,\ldots,p-1$, and their representation uses $\lceil\log_2p\rceil$ bits.

An exact output is the complete integer, finite list, or Laurent polynomial with its integer coefficients and exponents. A floating-point approximation is not an exact output. A field-operation count treats each addition, subtraction, multiplication, division by a nonzero element, and equality test in $\mathbb F_p$ as one operation; this convention does not assert that these operations have constant bit cost as $p$ varies.

before.title: Enumerate Reidemeister move neighbors from a knot code
before.statement:
**Input:** A valid normalized oriented planar-diagram code $C$ for a connected one-component knot diagram, with $c$ crossings. A positive-crossing-count code records its finite crossing labels, four darts at each crossing, edge pairings, clockwise rotations, strand orientations, over/under pairs, crossing signs, and one outer face. A crossingless code records one oriented circle and its outer face.

**Output:** A finite ordered list of pairs $(E,\mu)$, where $E$ is a valid normalized one-component knot code and $\mu$ records either the finite crossing/edge relabeling identifying the unchanged planar-isotopy class or a local disk boundary, move type, and orientation/sign variant witnessing one oriented R1, R2, or R3 move from $C$ to $E$. Different labelings of the same candidate may appear more than once.

**Finite comparison rules:** Two normalized codes represent the same code class when some bijection of their finite crossing labels and edge labels carries all dart incidences, crossing rotations, orientations, signs, component cycles, and outer-face data of one code to the other. To test whether two codes differ by one move, enumerate all finite choices of local edge intervals and crossing subrecords of sizes allowed by R1, R2, or R3; test that the codes agree outside the chosen disk boundary and that the two local records are one of the standard orientation/sign variants of that move. The local-site test uses the exact variants in the oriented Reidemeister-move definition.

**Instructions:**

1. Validate $C$ with the planar-code validation procedure. If it is invalid, return its first invalid-code result.
2. Set $N:=c+2$ and run the bounded normalized-diagram enumerator with bound $N$. It returns a finite list of reconstructed one-component knot-diagram candidates.
3. For each candidate, form the finite set of normalized code representatives obtained by assigning crossing labels and edge labels in every permitted order and applying the code's normalization rule.
4. For each representative $E$, apply the finite comparison rules. Append $E$ with a relabeling certificate if it is the same code class as $C$, or with the successful local-site certificate if a comparison certifies one R1, R2, or R3 move between them. Preserve the enumerator order and retain duplicates.
5. Return the accumulated list.

The bound $c+2$ includes every one-move result because R1 changes crossing count by one, R2 by two, and R3 by zero. This procedure lists candidates one move away; it does not decide whether two arbitrary codes are related by any number of moves.

after.title: Enumerate Reidemeister move neighbors from a knot code
after.statement:
**Input:** A valid normalized oriented planar-diagram code $C$ for a connected one-component knot diagram, with $c$ crossings. A positive-crossing-count code records its finite crossing labels, four darts at each crossing, edge pairings, clockwise rotations, strand orientations, over/under pairs, crossing signs, and one outer face. A crossingless code records one oriented circle and its outer face.

**Output:** A finite ordered list of pairs $(E,\mu)$, where $E$ is a valid normalized one-component knot code and $\mu$ records either the finite crossing/edge relabeling identifying the unchanged planar-isotopy class or a local disk boundary, move type, and orientation/sign variant witnessing one oriented R1, R2, or R3 move from $C$ to $E$. Different labelings of the same candidate may appear more than once.

**Finite comparison rules:** Two normalized codes represent the same code class when some bijection of their finite crossing labels and edge labels carries all dart incidences, crossing rotations, orientations, signs, component cycles, and outer-face data of one code to the other. For a move-site test use the finite spherical cellulation returned by reconstruction and mark a point at infinity in its distinguished outer face. For the crossingless circle, insert one auxiliary degree-two vertex and use its two complementary face disks; this vertex is suppressed in all comparisons.

For each of $m=2,4,6$, enumerate every distribution of $m$ distinct cut points among diagram edges and every linear order of the points on each edge. Use one representative of each order (for example equally spaced interior points); their numerical positions are immaterial. In each face disk enumerate noncrossing pairings of all boundary occurrences of these cut points by interior arcs. In the distinguished face also record which complementary region contains the marked point at infinity. Glue the face arcs at the cut points and retain only choices forming a single simple closed curve. Cutting the finite cellulation along these arcs and flooding across incident cell pieces identifies the two sides; select the side not containing infinity. This is the candidate closed move disk. Its entire diagram intersection, including every vertex, edge segment and possible closed component inside it, must be isomorphic relative to its cyclically ordered boundary points to one side of a standard R1, R2 or R3 template with the chosen orientation/sign variant. In particular no additional diagram portion is permitted inside the disk. All tests are finite incidence and cyclic-order comparisons. The same construction is performed for the other code, requiring the opposite side of the same template and an isomorphism of the outside records fixing the ordered boundary points, all decorations and the infinity region. Store the cut orders, face pairings, selected regions, template variant and outside isomorphism as the certificate.

The local templates and their exact orientation/sign variants are those in the oriented Reidemeister-move definition.

**Instructions:**

1. Validate $C$ with the planar-code validation procedure. If it is invalid, return its first invalid-code result.
2. Set $N:=c+2$ and run the bounded normalized-diagram enumerator with bound $N$. It returns a finite list of reconstructed one-component knot-diagram candidates.
3. For each candidate, form the finite set of normalized code representatives obtained by assigning crossing labels and edge labels in every permitted order and applying the code's normalization rule.
4. For each representative $E$, apply the finite comparison rules. Append $E$ with a relabeling certificate if it is the same code class as $C$, or with the successful local-site certificate if a comparison certifies one R1, R2, or R3 move between them. Preserve the enumerator order and retain duplicates.
5. Return the accumulated list.

The bound $c+2$ includes every one-move result because R1 changes crossing count by one, R2 by two, and R3 by zero. This procedure lists candidates one move away; it does not decide whether two arbitrary codes are related by any number of moves.

before.title: Connected-diagram bracket span bound and alternating equality
before.statement: For a connected regular link diagram $D$ with $c$ crossings, the Laurent-polynomial span of its Kauffman bracket is at most $4c$. If $D$ is reduced and alternating, then changing any one crossing from the all-$A$ state or the all-$B$ state merges two distinct state circles, both extreme coefficients are nonzero, and the bracket span is exactly $4c$. The span of a nonzero Laurent polynomial is its largest exponent minus its smallest exponent.
before.strategy: Bound state degrees by the all-A and all-B states, use the connected saddle surface to show the two extreme circle counts sum to at most c+2, then use checkerboard faces and reducedness to obtain equality and noncancelling extreme terms.

before.statement: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $K=K_1\#K_2$ be a smooth oriented connected sum with both factors nontrivial. Let $S$ be a regular level sphere giving a bridge position: $S$ divides $S^3$ into two balls, and in each ball the knot is a finite collection of properly embedded arcs, each of which cobounds an embedded disk with an arc on $S$; the disks in each ball are pairwise disjoint. Let $P$ be a smooth decomposing sphere meeting $K$ transversely in two points and cutting it into the given two oriented factors. Put $E=S^3\setminus\operatorname{int}N(K)$ and let $A=P\setminus\operatorname{int}N(K)$ be the resulting annulus, where $N(K)$ is a small closed tubular neighborhood. Assume the inclusion-induced map $\pi_1(A)\to\pi_1(E)$ is injective and that there is no embedded disk in $E$, with interior disjoint from $A\cup\partial E$, whose boundary is the union of a properly embedded arc in $A$ that does not cobound a disk in $A$ with a subarc of $\partial A$ and an arc in $\partial E$. Then, after isotoping $P$ through spheres meeting $K$ twice and changing only the bridge-spanning disk systems for the fixed pair $(K,S)$, one can arrange that $P\cap S$ is exactly one simple closed curve and that the union of the upper and lower bridge-spanning disks meets $P$ in exactly two arcs, each joining one point of $P\cap K$ to a point of $P\cap S$.

before.statement:
Let $F_r$ be the free group with Magnus expansion $E$, let $u,\lambda\in F_r$,
and let $w$ be a nonempty word of length $m$. The coefficient of $X_w$ in
$E(u^{-1}\lambda u)-E(\lambda)$ is an integer linear combination of
coefficients of $E(\lambda)$ on proper contiguous subwords of $w$. Thus, when
$w$ is the prefix of a Milnor index $I=(w,j)$, conjugating the longitude can
change its degree-$m$ coefficient only by an integer combination of
coefficients indexed by proper subsequences of $I$.

before.statement:
Assume AC. The input is either (a) a based $r$-component string-link diagram
with its endpoint collars and product-tube parallels equal to the diagram's
blackboard push-offs, or (b) a based finite regular
diagram of a closed $r$-component labeled oriented link with chosen product
tubes, one initial strand on each component, and a common basepoint and access
paths. In either mode require $r\geq1$. The finite input records its compatible common-upper-collar reference accesses. In the compatible branch the actual accesses are these, up to a common base-path change, and the parallels are the blackboard parallels already specified. In the arbitrary-choice branch it additionally records finite words in the compatible strand meridians for each access difference $g_e$, the parallel endpoint differences $h_{0,j},h_{1,j}$, and its relative meridian winding $k_j$. These are word certificates for the chosen paths, part of the supplied based-word data; no evaluation of an unencoded smooth path is claimed. In closed-link mode the preferred longitude uses its own recorded access $h_j$, which may differ from the initial-meridian access $g_j$. Arbitrary parallels are allowed in this branch, with the recorded $k_j$. The input also includes a maximum index length $N\geq2$. The output is
the integer coefficients $\mu_\tau(I)$ in string-link mode, or the based
coefficients $\mu_L^b(I)$, their lower indeterminacy data $\Delta_I^b$, and
residues $\bar\mu_L^b(I)$ in closed-link mode, for every index sequence $I$
with $2\leq |I|\leq N$.

Set $d=N-1$ and work in the truncated noncommutative ring
$$R_d=\mathbb Z\langle X_1,\ldots,X_r\rangle/\mathfrak m^{d+1},$$
where $\mathfrak m$ is the ideal generated by the letters. Carry out the
following finite procedure.

1. Verify the finite crossing, orientation, over/under, and component data. If
   a closed-link component has no underpassing point, choose a crossing-free
   disk meeting only a short arc of that component and avoiding its chosen
   initial meridian point. Insert a small type-I curl there by the supported
   disk isotopy and record the resulting based diagram. Transport the
   basepoint, meridian circles, access paths, product tubes, parallels, and all
   supplied access, endpoint, and longitude word certificates through this
   isotopy. Before the curl, the component is one cyclic strand; the new
   underpass cuts it into one interval strand containing the chosen initial
   point. Identify that interval's reference meridian symbol with the
   transported old symbol. Every other strand is carried bijectively by the
   isotopy, with its reference symbol identified in the same way. In the finite
   certificates, apply this symbol substitution to every word; no unencoded
   path evaluation or additional certificate is required. Give every
   resulting strand $a$ the component label $j(a)$.

2. First compute in the compatible reference root symbols $x_j$, irrespective of the actual access choices. For every strand $a$, initialize its meridian series by
   $Y_a^{(1)}=1+X_{j(a)}$. For each degree $\ell=2,\ldots,d$, copy every
   $Y_a^{(\ell-1)}$ into the constant and lower-degree part of
   $Y_a^{(\ell)}$, with new degree-$\ell$ terms initially zero, and reset each
   chosen root strand to $1+X_j$. Then do one pass over each component in its
   oriented order. In closed-link mode start at the chosen initial strand and
   omit the final undercrossing back to that strand; in string-link mode start
   at the bottom endpoint and use every undercrossing through to the top
   endpoint. At an undercrossing with over-strand $o$ and source and target
   under-arcs $s,t$, use the already available $Y_o^{(\ell-1)}$ and the
   current $Y_s^{(\ell)}$ to set
   $$Y_t^{(\ell)}=\operatorname{trunc}_{\ell}\bigl((Y_o^{(\ell-1)})^{-1} Y_s^{(\ell)}Y_o^{(\ell-1)}\bigr)$$
   when the traversal is source-to-target, and set
   $$Y_s^{(\ell)}=\operatorname{trunc}_{\ell}\bigl(Y_o^{(\ell-1)} Y_t^{(\ell)}(Y_o^{(\ell-1)})^{-1}\bigr)$$
   when it is target-to-source. Here $\operatorname{trunc}_{\ell}$ discards
   monomials of degree greater than $\ell$, and every inverse is the finite
   geometric series in the nilpotent ideal of $R_d$.

3. For each component $j$, traverse its undercrossings in order and form
   $W_j=\prod_c (Y_{o(c)}^{(d)})^{\epsilon_c}$, where the factors are in
   traversal order and $\epsilon_c=+1$ for source-to-target and $-1$ for
   target-to-source. In string-link mode set $\Lambda_j=W_j$. In closed-link
   mode set
   $$\Lambda_j=(1+X_j)^{-\operatorname{wr}_j(D)}W_j,$$
   where $\operatorname{wr}_j(D)$ is the sum of the determinant signs at
   self-crossings of component $j$.

4. In the arbitrary-choice branch first use the strand-symbol identification of step 1, then evaluate each supplied transport word by the strand series from step 2.    $$H_{0,j}(1+X_j)^{k_j}W_jH_{1,j}^{-1}.$$
   In closed-link mode replace the compatible preferred series by
   $$H_j(1+X_j)^{-\operatorname{wr}_j(D)}W_jH_j^{-1},$$
   where $H_j=H_{0,j}=H_{1,j}$ is the actual longitude access difference, independently of the initial-meridian difference $G_j$. The arbitrary parallel winding cancels in the preferred correction. All powers and inverses are finite truncated operations. To express this result in the actual component-meridian symbols, form
   $$G_j(1+X_j)G_j^{-1}=1+X_j+R_j(X),\qquad \deg R_j\ge2.$$
   With new letters $V_j$, initialize $Z_j^{(1)}=V_j$ and iterate
   $$Z_j^{(s+1)}=\operatorname{trunc}_d\bigl(V_j-R_j(Z^{(s)})\bigr),\qquad 1\le s<d.$$
   Substitute $X_j=Z_j^{(d)}(V)$ in the corrected longitude series. This is its expansion in the chosen actual meridians. For the compatible branch this step is the identity. Rename the final letters $V_j$ as $X_j$.

5. For every $I=(i_1,\ldots,i_k,j)$ with $1\leq k\leq d$, read the coefficient
   of $X_{i_1}\cdots X_{i_k}$ in $\Lambda_j$. In string-link mode return this
   integer. In closed-link mode, also compute the gcd of the coefficients for
   all proper subsequences of cyclic permutations of $I$ of lengths at least
   two, with empty gcd equal to zero, and return the corresponding residue
   class.

All scans, including the supplied transport words and the $d-1$ inverse-substitution iterations, are over finite crossing, strand, degree, and index sets. The
procedure makes no polynomial-time claim. If a finite-input validation fails,
return `invalid-input`.

before.title: Isotopy invariance and nonrepeating link-homotopy scope of Milnor invariants

references.title: John Milnor, Link Groups
references.locator: §§4–5, PDF pp. 14–16, link-homotopy and Milnor coefficient discussion

references.title: Ryan Stees, Milnor’s Invariants for Knots and Links in Closed Orientable 3-Manifolds
references.locator: §2.5, printed pp. 16–18 (PDF pp. 24–26), based coefficients and closed-link residues

before.statement:
Assume AC. Every integer Milnor coefficient of a based string link is invariant
under smooth isotopy through string links fixing the endpoint collars. For
closed labeled oriented links, the residue candidate $\bar\mu_L(I)$ is invariant
under ambient isotopy. A link-homotopy is a finite sequence of ambient isotopies
and local crossing changes in which the two branches at every crossing change
belong to the same component. Under link-homotopy, $\bar\mu_L(I)$ is invariant
when the entries of $I$ are pairwise distinct. No invariance for repeated-index
sequences under link-homotopy is asserted.

before.title: A dualizable link can slide off a meridian disk

references.title: Lisa Piccirillo, The Conway knot is not slice
references.locator: Theorem 3.1 proof, §3, arXiv v1 PDF p. 4, finite slides removing intersections with $D_R$

references.title: Jennifer Hom, Getting a handle on the Conway knot
references.locator: §3, dualizable-link cancellation argument

before.statement:
Assume countable choice. Let $(B,G,R)$ be a dualizable framed handle link, and
isotope $R$ to an unknot bounding a disk $D_R$ that meets $B$ transversely in
one point. Then there is a finite sequence of slides of the $2$-handle $G$ over
the $2$-handle $B$, together with link isotopies, after which the attaching
circle for $G$ is disjoint from $D_R$.

before.title: The exterior of a slice disk has first homology generated by a meridian

references.title: Lisa Piccirillo, The Conway knot is not slice
references.locator: Lemma 1.3 proof, the disk-core cone construction, printed p. 583 (PDF p. 2)

references.title: Allen Hatcher, Algebraic Topology
references.locator: §2.2, excision and relative homology sequences

before.statement:
Let $D\subset B^4$ be a smooth properly embedded disk with boundary knot
$K\subset S^3=\partial B^4$. Choose a product tubular neighborhood
$\nu(D)\cong D^2\times D^2$ whose intersection with $S^3$ is the chosen tube
$N(K)$, and let $X=\overline{B^4\setminus\operatorname{int}\nu(D)}$. Then the
inclusion $E_K\hookrightarrow X$ induces an isomorphism
$$H_1(E_K;\mathbb Z)\xrightarrow{\cong}H_1(X;\mathbb Z)$$
carrying the positive meridian of $K$ to the positive normal-circle generator.

before.title: A knot is smoothly slice exactly when its zero-trace embeds in $S^4$

references.title: Lisa Piccirillo, The Conway knot is not slice
references.locator: Lemma 1.3 and its complete two-direction proof, printed p. 583 (PDF p. 2)

references.title: Jennifer Hom, Getting a handle on the Conway knot
references.locator: §2.1, trace-embedding lemma and proof discussion

before.statement:
Let $K\subset S^3$ be a smooth oriented knot with a chosen tubular neighborhood
and preferred longitude. Call $K$ smoothly slice when it bounds a smooth
properly embedded disk in the standard $B^4$, with a product collar at its
boundary. Then $K$ is smoothly slice if and only if the compact smooth
$4$-manifold $X_0(K)$, formed using that preferred-longitude framing, admits a
smooth codimension-zero embedding into the standard $S^4$.

before.title: The unknot zero-trace and a dualizable cancellation diagram

references.title: Lisa Piccirillo, The Conway knot is not slice
references.locator: Definition 1.2 and the dualizable-link cancellation in Theorem 3.1, §3, arXiv v1 PDF p. 4

references.title: Jennifer Hom, Getting a handle on the Conway knot
references.locator: §2.1, trace of the unknot as a disk neighborhood

before.statement:
Assume countable choice. Let $U$ be the standard unknot. Its zero-trace is
diffeomorphic to $S^2\times D^2$ and embeds in the standard $S^4$ as a tubular
neighborhood of an unknotted $S^2$. It also has the following dualizable-link
description: take a dotted unknot $R$ and two zero-framed meridian circles
$B,G$ at distinct points of $R$, with their normal spanning disks disjoint.
Then $B\cup R$ and $G\cup R$ are meridional pairs, $\operatorname{lk}(B,G)=0$,
and cancelling either meridional $1$–$2$ pair leaves the zero-framed unknot
trace.
